# Feature status

[한국어](features.ko.md)

Validation applies to the stated implementation only. Passing tests does not mean a change was released.

Host diagnostic input (`input.pointer`, `input.key`) must reach the application through the same dispatch as a person's mouse and keyboard. It does not yet: keys go to `-[NSWindow sendEvent:]` and skip the menu key equivalents that `-[NSApplication sendEvent:]` runs, and pointer presses, drags, and releases call the hit view directly. This is a defect of the diagnostic input, recorded as V5-45.

## Active implementation checklist

This is the canonical task checklist; the Korean file is its translation, not another work queue. `[ ]` means waiting, `[~]` means active, `[o]` means the stated acceptance criteria have current evidence, and `[!]` records a temporary bypass. Historical passes below do not validate later changes. The [verification contract](spec/verification.md) defines the gates.

Completed entries and their scoped evidence are historical records; follow-up items identify later corrections without changing the original evidence.

- [o] F0.4-1-1 — P0: Make sidecar output failures observable to pages, derived from F0.4-1. The Wails stdio reader ended silently on a line over its 16 MiB scanner limit without checking `scanner.Err()`, both hosts logged an invalid JSON line and continued, Tauri only logged a read error or output close, Wails only cleaned up on output end, and Tauri read lines without a bound. Contract: a stdio sidecar message has at most 64 MiB before its newline in both hosts, enforced while reading; an oversize line, an invalid message, a read error, or an output end outside stop terminates the process and delivers `sidecar-failure` `{sidecar, surface, reason}` to each owning window of a surface that sent to it; the next send starts a new process; pages receive failures through `onFailure`, and the workbench reports an unhandled failure as a page error. Red on the unchanged readers: Wails `TestSidecarMessageAtTheLimitIsDelivered` failed with `no sidecar event within 10s`, and `TestOversizeSidecarMessageTerminatesAndNotifies`, `TestInvalidSidecarMessageTerminatesAndNotifies`, and `TestSidecarOutputCloseNotifiesEachSurface` failed with `no sidecar failure within 10s`; Tauri `an_oversize_message_terminates_and_notifies`, `an_invalid_message_terminates_and_notifies`, and `an_output_close_notifies_each_surface` failed with `no sidecar failure within 10s` while `a_message_at_the_limit_is_delivered` passed because the reader had no bound; the JS tests failed with `onFailure is not a function`, no installed `sidecar-failure` listener, and a `sidecarSend` before the listener. Green: `go test ./packages/host/wailsv3/...` passes, `cargo test -p soksak-host-tauriv2` passes 131 tests, `make host-contract-check` passes 240 of 240 cases in both hosts (Wails 141 tests, Tauri 142 tests), plugin-api 113, Wails runtime 9, Tauri runtime 10, and workbench 200 tests pass, and `make boundaries`, `make exposure-check`, and `make docs-check` pass.
- [o] F0.4-1-1-1 — P1: Distinguish a sidecar message for a removed surface from a message for a surface that never had an owner. Cause: both hosts drop a message whose surface has no owner. After the host sends `closed`, the sidecar can still send for that surface, so the drop is a legitimate post-close race, but the stdio protocol has no close acknowledgement that would let the host know when the race ends; a message for an unknown surface is therefore dropped without a report. Acceptance: the protocol declares when a closed surface can no longer receive messages, the host reports a message for a surface that is neither owned nor in that window as a sidecar failure, and both host tests show the post-close message discarded and the unknown-surface message reported. Done on 2026-10-02: `sidecars.md` states that the host remembers every surface it has sent to a stdio sidecar process until the process ends, discards a message for such a surface without an owning window, and fails the sidecar with `unknown surface <surface>` for a surface it never sent to that process; the persistent transport keeps sessions across application processes and keeps discarding. Both hosts already kept the addressed surfaces of each process, so no close acknowledgement was needed. Red: `TestClosedSurfaceMessagesAreDiscardedAndUnknownOnesFail` and `closed_surface_messages_are_discarded_and_unknown_ones_fail` received the s1 message after the discarded s2 message but no failure (`the test stalled`). Green: both host test suites, `make host-contract-check` (Wails 289/289, Tauri 295/295), and the shell and files window checks (14 of 14 on both rebuilt debug hosts) with no `unknown surface` line in the host logs.
- [o] F0.4-1-1-2 — P1: Apply the message limit and failure rules to the persistent sidecar transport. Cause: the persistent readers read lines without a bound in both hosts, and the Wails persistent reader logs an invalid surface event and continues while the Tauri reader disconnects. Acceptance: terminal runtime declares the persistent message limit and the outcome of an invalid event, both hosts enforce the same outcome while reading, and host contract cases cover an oversize and an invalid persistent event. Done on 2026-10-02: `terminal-runtime.md` applies the stdio message limit to every line of the service connection and makes an oversize line, a non-object line, a reply field of the wrong type or a surface event without a string `surface` and a `body` end the connection with `sidecar-failure` to each surface that has sent, without an immediate reconnection; the next send reconnects. Before, both hosts read lines without a bound, Wails logged an invalid surface event and continued, and both hosts treated an invalid line as a connection loss and reconnected at once. Red: the new tests on both hosts waited for a failure that never came (`no sidecar failure; the test stalled`). Green: `make host-contract-check` (Wails 288/288, Tauri 294/294). The Tauri reply checks now use the Go wording for a failed reply without an error text (`retained failed`).
- [o] F0.4-1-1-3 — P2: Measure the 64 MiB limit-message delivery under load. In the first host contract check after merging F0.4-1-1 into `main` (2026-10-01, load average about 13 on 11 processors), the Wails test `TestSidecarMessageAtTheLimitIsDelivered` failed with `no sidecar event within 10s`; five isolated runs, three runs of the sidecar group through `make go-repeat` and a second contract check passed, the test taking 2.8–2.9 s. Retry when it fails again: record the elapsed time and load of each run through `make go-repeat` and decide whether the delivery or the wait is wrong. The Tauri test `a_message_at_the_limit_is_delivered` failed the same way (`no sidecar event within 10s`) in the diagnostics run of a host contract check on 2026-10-01 at load average 56–61 on 11 processors, while other checks shared the machine. Decision on 2026-10-02: the wait was wrong and the delivery is correct. At load average 31–33 on 11 processors the message was delivered on every run, in 10.7, 11.9 and 19.0 s on Wails and 6.1, 9.7 and 15.0 s on Tauri (2.8 s at low load), so the time grows with the load and a 10 s wait judged a correct delivery as a failure. G1.4-38 replaced the wait with the received event and a bound that only ends a stalled test.

      - [o] G1.4-14-4-2 — P1: Measure the divider alignment again under normal load. On 2026-10-01 the outside alignment check showed layouts 43–65 ms (Wails) and 37–46 ms (Tauri) after the grid left them, against the specified 34 ms (two 60 Hz frames), while two `mysqld` processes used about 97% CPU each, a virtual machine about 69%, and the five-minute load average was about 19 on 11 processors. In the failing frames the native commits follow each step within 4–8 ms, and the card shows a DOM layout three steps old, so the app DOM paint is late. Retry when the load average is below the processor count; a failure then needs owning Red in the presentation path. Retried 2026-10-01 at a load average of 3.8–4.1 on 11 processors without the `mysqld` processes: the check still fails on both rebuilt hosts, with the card showing a layout 53.7 ms (Wails) and 48.5 ms (Tauri) after the grid left it and medians of 36.3 ms and 30.5 ms at 60 Hz, so the lag is not caused by load. The app DOM presentation takes two to three 60 Hz frames per step; the next step is owning Red in the presentation path (the placement waits for the next app DOM presentation). Measurement: the page now traces every layout's stages (`layout` events with `queued`, `prepare`, `prepared`, `draw`, `drawn`, `frame`, `presented` and `performance.now()` times). On both hosts at 60Hz the waiting for the previous layout takes a median 6–7 ms (p90 13 ms), the native preparation 3–4 ms, the DOM drawing 1 ms and the wait for the next animation frame 11–12 ms; the native transaction commits 5–8 ms after each step. The delay comes from frame boundaries, not computation: a layout reaches the screen across the input's arrival, the frame of the previous layout, WebKit's rendering update and the display refresh, so it is bounded by four display frames; at 120Hz that bound was within the old 34 ms, at 60Hz it is 66.7 ms. Eight runs per host gave medians of 20–35 ms, 90th percentiles of 27–45 ms and worst values of 34–49 ms at a load average of 8–9, and 63–66 ms at 10. Decision (2026-10-01): the user found the present drag delay acceptable and asked for a criterion strict enough to catch regressions; the old 34 ms limit had never held at 60Hz with this presentation order, which keeps native content and cards aligned. Criterion: in display frames from `host.window.refreshRate`, the worst delay at most 4 frames, the median at most 2.5 frames and the 90th percentile at most 3 frames, so a one-frame regression of the usual delay fails; docs/spec/native-surfaces.md states the rule. Green: the outside alignment check passes 2/2 on each rebuilt debug host (Wails median 26.6–31.6 ms, p90 40.4–44.2 ms, worst 46.8–51.6 ms; Tauri median 24.0–26.2 ms, p90 41.3–43.5 ms, worst 46.7–56.6 ms) (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, 60Hz).

  - [o] G1.4-101 — P1: End the web content process of each closed webview. Reported on 2026-10-03 at 20:20 by the user with an Activity Monitor capture (about twenty `wails://localhost` and `tauri://localhost` processes); measured at 23:00: each check application showed its main page and one browser document region (`host.window` webviews 2 on each host), so four web content processes were in use, while twenty web content processes started at or after the check applications' start at 20:16 were still running about three hours later. Reproduce it with a tracked check that opens and closes webviews and counts the web content processes the application started. Measured on 2026-10-03 between 23:05 and 23:55: the counts did not fall after 35 idle minutes, so the processes are not the WebKit process cache, whose cached processes live 30 minutes; opening and closing a browser card three times, a main-page reload and three settings openings left the counts unchanged; opening and closing a project window twice added two `WebPageProxy` objects per window on both hosts (Wails 23 to 27, Tauri 24 to 28). `heap` on the check applications showed the objects of every closed window still allocated: on Tauri 12 `TaoWindow`, 11 `WryWebView` and 12 each of `SPWindowComposition`, `SPSurfaceCoordinates`, `SPFileDropView` and `SPOcclusionObserver` with one open window; on Wails 11 `WebviewWindowDelegate` and 9 `WKWebView`; on both 18 `SPSurfaceHost` and 34 `SPSurfaceNativePlane`. A closed window and its webviews are not deallocated, so their web content processes keep running. Causes, read on 2026-10-04 from the code and from the framework sources and reproduced by tracked tests: (1) neither host closed the logical surfaces, document regions, and image regions of a closing window. The Tauri `Destroyed` handler (`packages/host/tauriv2/src/windows.rs`) closed none, and the Wails `Surfaces.close` (`packages/host/wailsv3/src/windows.go`) closed only the webviews in `nativeViews`, while logical surfaces are kept in `s.views`. Each surface holds the main webview (`SPSurfaceHost.mainWebview` in `native/darwin/src/webview_geometry.m`) through the handle that `sp_surface_create` gives the host, and each document region is a webview with its own web content process that its handle keeps. The main webview, its configuration (on Wails with the `WebviewWindowDelegate` that is its URL scheme handler), the surface and plane views, and every open document region therefore stayed with their web content processes. (2) `webviewInputRegister` (`native/darwin/src/webview_input.m`) added a script message handler to the webview's `WKUserContentController` and removed it only in `webviewInputUnregister`, which neither host calls for the main webview or for modal webviews. WebKit keeps a controller while a handler is registered, so the controller and its handlers stayed after the webview was released. (3) The file drop receiver that each host passes to `sp_window_file_drop` was never freed (Tauri `Box::into_raw` in `packages/host/tauriv2/src/platform/darwin/webview.rs`, Wails `cgo.NewHandle` in `packages/host/wailsv3/src/platform/darwin/webview.go`), so a `tauri::Window` clone and the Wails `Surfaces` of every closed window stayed. The framework sources at the pinned versions release their window references on close: Wails v3.0.0-beta.16 creates `WebviewWindow` with the default `releasedWhenClosed` and closes it with `close`; tao 0.37.0 sets `releasedWhenClosed` to false and holds the `NSWindow` only in `UnownedWindow` and its delegate state, which tauri-runtime-wry rev 270c63f drops when it removes the window on `Destroyed`; wry 0.56.1 removes its IPC handler and the webview from its superview when the webview is dropped; a `tauri::Window` clone holds the window id and the shared runtime context, not the tao window. The other receivers that the Tauri host passes with `Box::into_raw` (document and image regions, pointer input, activation, capture, the UI queue) are freed when the region closes or when the one-shot callback runs. The library test does not reproduce the retention of the `NSWindow` and `SPWindowComposition` that `heap` measured on Tauri; the rebuilt applications must show whether it remains and what holds it. Fix: both hosts close each surface's document regions and image regions and then the surface when the window closes (`close_window_surfaces` and `CloseWindowSurfaces`, host contract cases `window-close.surfaces.*`); an input registration is an associated object of the webview that removes the handler when the registration ends or the webview is released; `sp_window_file_drop` takes a release function that the drop view calls for a replaced receiver and when the view is released, and both hosts free the receiver there. Red: `native/darwin/tests/window_release_test.m` failed `the closed window releases its main WKUserContentController` and `the closed window releases its modal WKUserContentController` against the unchanged library, and, with the release parameter added but not called, failed `a replaced file drop receiver is released once (released ())` and `the closed window releases its file drop receiver once (released ())`. `packages/host/tauriv2/tests/window_close_test.rs` and `packages/host/wailsv3/tests/window_close_test.go`, run against a function that closed nothing as the unchanged close paths did, failed both cases with an empty close list (`left: []`, `closed []`). Cause in tao 0.37.1: `src/platform_impl/macos/window.rs:247-255` retains the window that `alloc` and `initWithContentRect:` already returned owned, and `releasedWhenClosed` is off, so nothing releases it; the hand-written `dealloc` of `TaoView` (`view.rs:266`) and `TaoWindowDelegate` (`window_delegate.rs:282`) does not call `[super dealloc]`. Correction on 2026-10-04: the first Green run of `window-release.test.mjs` with the pin failed on both hosts with one `windowCompositions` left (Wails 1 to 2 with the other counts unchanged; Tauri 1 to 2 and `inputRegistrations` 2 to 3), and a count taken later showed the starting values, so the check read the counts before the release and the merged check was wrong. Two causes were measured. AppKit keeps a window that was on screen until its close animation ends: the native test with the window ordered front failed `the closed window and its webviews leave the counts at {windowCompositions 1, surfaceHosts 0, inputRegistrations 1}` against the unchanged library and passed with `animationBehavior` set to none, and the counts of both applications returned about 270 ms after the close. In the Tauri host the composition is released one event iteration later still: a debugger trace showed `-[NSApplication run]` draining its pool, releasing the autoreleased `TaoView`, whose `dealloc` removes its subviews and autoreleases the composition (`-[NSView _removeSubview:]`), which the next drain releases; with no event after the close the composition stayed for 2 s and more. `sp_window_objects_after_event` is replaced by `sp_window_objects_when(expected, seconds, done, context)`: while a request waits, the library posts one application-defined event each time the main run loop is about to wait and compares the counts after each such event is handled, because no event reports an object that waits in an autorelease pool; it gives the counts and `reached` false when the bound of 10 seconds ends. `diagnostics.native.objects` accepts `equal`, the window check passes the counts from before the first open, and both hosts check `equal` and the failure text alike (host contract case `diagnostics.native-objects.equal-validates`). What the hosts do with an explicit `null` in a numeric field follows their decoders: Go's `encoding/json` leaves the field unchanged (0) without an error, while serde refuses `null` for `f64`; that host difference is G1.4-105-1. Measure the texts of both hosts for a malformed argument and give them one text with a host contract case. Done on 2026-10-04: both hosts decode every argument with their own decoder before the call runs, so neither framework decodes an argument: the Wails `Host` bindings and native calls take raw JSON and call `decodeArgument` (`packages/host/wailsv3/src/arguments.go`, replacing `binding_json.go`), and every Tauri command argument other than a framework object is `Argument<T>` (`packages/host/tauriv2/src/arguments.rs`, a serde deserializer over the JSON value). Tauri (`serde_json::from_value`): a workspace `project` of 5 was accepted, and the other refusals had serde texts such as `missing field `surfaces`` and `invalid length 3, expected an array of length 4`. The tracked cases `null status value` and `missing status value` (Go) and the `Changed` case (Rust) failed with that message, and pass after the status value became optional in both hosts. Reported on 2026-10-04 by the user: after the window checks the check applications' main page processes held 446.6 MB (Wails) and 399.9 MB (Tauri) against about 70 MB for a newly started release build, and G1.4-101 had been reported as the leak fix although it covers only closed windows. Cause (G1.4-64-1-4, read again in the WebKit source of `main` on 2026-10-04): `Document::m_querySelectorAllResults` keeps the `NodeList` of each cacheable `querySelectorAll`, the list holds the elements and the elements hold the document, so a replaced document stays until a DOM change under the queried node removes the entry or `releaseCriticalMemory` calls `clearQuerySelectorAllResults` under memory pressure; document teardown does not clear it. WebKit offers no interface that releases this for one web content process except testing SPI (`_processWillSuspendForTesting:`), and `org.WebKit.lowMemory` reaches every WebKit process of the system. G1.4-64-1-3 kept the page process on reload and left the cache to WebKit, which this item reopens. Measure the growth per reload and per page change on a release build (G1.4-102), then remove the retention. Measured on 2026-10-04 (macOS 26.6.2) in a scratch WKWebView program, not yet a tracked test: a navigation delegate that answers `_WKNavigationActionPolicyAllowInNewProcess` for the main frame moved both `reload` and a load of the same file URL to a new web content process every time, and the previous process ended for reloads; for loads it stayed alive (back/forward suspended page) until `-[WKWebView _clearBackForwardCache]` and `-[WKProcessPool _clearWebProcessCache]` were called. Next: put this decision in `native/darwin` for both hosts, a tracked native test (Red: the reload keeps the process and the cached document), and `window-release`-style process exit checks for page reloads and page changes. Done on 2026-10-04: the shared library wraps the navigation delegate of the app DOM webview when `sp_window_set_main_webview` registers it (`native/darwin/src/webview_navigation.m`, both hosts without host changes): the framework delegate still receives every message, an allowed main-frame navigation that replaces the document is answered with `_WKNavigationActionPolicyAllowInNewProcess`, and each commit calls `_clearBackForwardCache`, so the previous process ends with the replaced document; a fragment navigation keeps its process. This reverses the G1.4-64-1-3 decision to keep the page process on reload; WebKit keeps the previous page on screen until the new one commits, and `page changes keep the window drawn` measured 0 undrawn frames for the reload and the library visit on both hosts. Red: `webview_navigation_test` failed with `reload 1 opens the document in a new WebContent process (68916 -> 68916)` against the unchanged library.     - [o] G1.4-64-1-4 — P1: Find what keeps a replaced main document alive, before G1.4-64-1-3 removes the forced process end. Cause, from the WebKit source and measured on 2026-10-03 (macOS 26.6.2, WebKit 21624.5.1.11.3): `Document` keeps the results of cacheable `querySelectorAll` calls in `m_querySelectorAllResults`; the result `NodeList` holds the elements, the elements hold the document, and teardown does not clear the map, so a reload in the same WebContent process leaves the previous document until WebKit's memory-pressure release calls `clearQuerySelectorAllResults`. `webview_process_test` reproduces it with one class query (about 55 MB of a document-owned marker kept per reload; none without the query; two consecutive repeat runs). On the application page, invalidating every cached result at page hide left one document after six reloads instead of seven, and WebKit's simulated memory warning returned seven documents to one and the footprint from 267 MB to 106 MB. The cause is in WebKit and the application cannot clear the cache for one process without simulating memory pressure; G1.4-64-1-3 keeps the page process and leaves the cache to WebKit's memory-pressure release. `diagnostics.page.collect` collects JavaScript objects before memory measurements.
    - [o] G1.4-64-1-5 — P1: Measure the first frames of a new window and show it only with its first screen. This item first stated that a recording starts only on an existing window and needs a new diagnostic; that was wrong: `diagnostics.capture.start {display: true}` already records every window of the application on the display, which the endpoint specification did not list and now does. Red: the new `e2e/window-first-frames.test.mjs` records the display while `core.window.new` opens a window and counts frames in which the window has appeared without its content; both hosts failed with empty frames from 254 ms (Wails) and 162 ms (Tauri) after the start of the recording, the window background and buttons alone while the window opened. Cause, from the WebKit source: WebKit draws a web view only while its window is on screen, and `WebViewImpl::windowDidOrderOnScreen` changes the activity state asynchronously, so a window shown before its page drew opens empty; showing a hidden window at the end of its first navigation still left five empty frames. Correction: the native-host specification states the order; `native/darwin` adds `sp_window_reveal_after_load`, which makes the window transparent and makes it opaque after the main webview's first load ends, successfully or not, and the presentation update after it; both hosts create every window hidden (Tauri `visible(false)` and `tauri.conf.json`), call it and then show the window. `window_reveal_test` covers the rejection without a main webview, the order, the page colour of the revealed window and a failed load. Green: the same check passes on both rebuilt debug hosts with 0 undrawn frames, and `e2e/library.test.mjs` passes (macOS 26.6.2 arm64).

Observed on 2026-10-03: `repeated reload keeps the host and the released page memory bounded` failed once on Wails with a footprint 165 MB above the start after 20 collect-and-measure attempts, and passed on the next run only at the 18th attempt. Reasons for the changed criterion: the released page footprint measures whether WebKit's memory-pressure release has emptied its `querySelectorAll` result cache, which is WebKit behaviour that `webview_process_test` reproduces at its owning module; WebKit offers no release for one process (the `WKWebView`, `WKProcessPool`, `WKWebsiteDataStore` and `_WKProcessPoolConfiguration` methods list none), so the check posted `org.WebKit.lowMemory`, which every WebKit process of the computer receives and which the private native API inventory already excluded as simulated memory pressure; and the release ends without an event, so the check was judged by an attempt count. Correction: `repeated reload keeps the host memory and the window documents bounded` keeps the host RSS bound and the unchanged page process, waits on `host.window` until the window holds the same number of webviews, the same surfaces and the same number of documents and image regions as before the 20 reloads, and records the page footprint without judging it. Sensitivity: a Wails build that removed documents from the registry without closing their native webviews failed the check with `the window documents differ from {"webviews":3,...}`; a build without `reloadSurfaceDocuments` failed earlier in the fixture with `image "view" is already attached`, and a build without the registry close at page start passed because `surfaceCommitted` closes the same documents. Green: the check passes on both rebuilt debug hosts (macOS 26.6.2 arm64).

A transcript of a 10-step divider drag shows one preparation (`syncSurfaces`), one drawn commit, and one `presentSurfaces` per step, 20 steps in about 400ms on both hosts, so the layout pipeline keeps pace with the pointer steps. Recordings (V5-12) show the DOM card and rail moving on every step while the browser document region, a separate WKWebView, trails the DOM by one to two steps while the layout moves and aligns again at rest. The native geometry is committed after the main document confirms presentation, and WebKit draws the DOM in its own process, so holding the window's layer transaction does not hold the DOM change; `-[NSWindow disableScreenUpdatesUntilFlush]` at the start of each preparation did not change the result. The alignment recording last passed at `ae687ce` (F1.1), before surfaces moved into the app DOM with document regions. Remaining: a design that shows DOM and native geometry in the same frame, then its regression and correction. Done on 2026-09-24: two causes were measured, and both came from `dcbca83` (F1.3-1). (1) The layout queue ran every waiting layout in arrival order. A presentation waits for the next app DOM presentation, which is at least one display frame, and pointer steps arrive every 16ms, so waiting layouts accumulated and the cards trailed the pointer by up to 100–140ms. The queue again keeps only the newest waiting layout, as step 5 of the placement sequence states; a replaced layout runs neither its preparation nor its draw, and the page writes the number of replaced layouts to the application log when the presentation settles. (2) The rail outline read the grid, which already holds the next prepared layout, while the cards show the layout of the last draw, so the rail led the cards by up to 25px. `SoksakView.painted(id)` now returns the rectangle the last draw wrote, and the rail uses it. After these corrections the worst drag delay was about 56ms on Wails and 62–94ms on Tauri: WebKit enables `PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPSEnabled` by default, so the app DOM updated its rendering near 60fps and each placement waited for that rendering. Registration of the app DOM webview now disables this WebKit feature and fails when the feature is missing; `host.window` reports `near60fps` per webview. `native content, cards, and the sidebar rail stay aligned` now also measures the delay: the host records each step time on the recording clock (`ticks`), the page reports the grid boundary after each step (`boundary`), and every recorded frame must show a layout at most 50ms after the grid left it. Red: the old builds failed on the rail at frame 17 (Wails) and 15 (Tauri); with the queue and rail corrections the delay failed at 50.8ms and 60.8ms; `window_facts_test` failed without the setting. Green on rebuilt Wails and Tauri: 10 of 10 tracked repeats passed with a worst delay of 18.7–26.8ms in the measured runs; `three terminals survive repeated divider drags and project returns` and `shell divider drag does not leave a white surface frame` passed, so the replaced waiting layouts did not remove the round-trip end states. A 34ms limit fails the first drag after an application start (37.8–39.4ms); reaching it is registered as F8-6-2.

The settle step behind `host.window.presented` forces DOM layout with `evaluateJavaScript` and waits for the next display frame; it does not wait for the web content process to commit the rendering of that DOM, which is what the [exposure specification](spec/exposure.md) promises. - [o] F14 — P1: Answer the operating system's quit request in the Wails host without cancelling it. Found on 2026-10-04: `tell application id "app.soksak.wails.dev" to quit` returned `-128` (user cancelled) although the application then ended, while the Tauri host ended without an error. The Wails framework (v3.0.0-beta.27, `application_darwin_delegate.m`) replies `NSTerminateCancel` when `ShouldQuit` returns false, and `shouldQuit` returns false while ready windows save; a cancelled reply can also stop a logout or a restart. The host must defer the reply until the saves finish, as the Tauri host does. Found on 2026-10-04 while checking the Tauri host: tao (the pinned fork `1a047e2`) does not implement `applicationShouldTerminate:`, so an operating system quit request ends the Tauri application through `applicationWillTerminate:` without the page-save wait that `RunEvent::ExitRequested` runs; whether pending saves are lost there is part of this item. Completed on 2026-10-04: the framework quit paths cannot defer the answer (Wails replies `NSTerminateCancel` and offers no later reply; tao has no `applicationShouldTerminate:`), so `native/darwin/src/quit_request.m` installs a handler of the `kAEQuitApplication` Apple event with the public `NSAppleEventManager` interface: it suspends the event and calls the host, which runs the same quit as `host.quit`, and `sp_quit_request_answer` resumes the event without an error in the shutdown step (Wails `OnShutdown`, Tauri `RunEvent::Exit`) after the saves ([hosts](spec/hosts.md)). Red: `quit_request_test` failed with "the request runs once on the main thread (0)" and "the quit event does not reach applicationShouldTerminate: (1 calls)" against an installation that installed nothing; on the earlier debug builds `tell application id "app.soksak.wails.dev" to quit` returned `-128`. Green: `make -C native/darwin repeat TEST=quit_request_test COUNT=3` passes; rebuilt debug applications with a ready main window answered the same request with status 0 in 0.15 s (Wails) and 0.14 s (Tauri), and both processes had ended when the answer arrived; `make platforms hosts-check host-parity-check docs-check parity-check`, the Go host tests, the Tauri host tests and the format and clippy checks pass. Platform: macOS 26 arm64.
- [o] F15 — P1: Report a malformed `process.lock` with the same text in both hosts. Found on 2026-10-04 while reading the lock code for R2-8: the Wails host reports `invalid process lock <path>` for any unreadable or non-positive PID, while the Tauri host reports `<path>: invalid process lock `<contents>`: <reason>` and `<path>: process lock contains PID 0`; the endpoint specification calls malformed locks errors without a shared text, and no contract case compares them. Completed on 2026-10-04: both hosts report a lock whose contents are not a positive process ID, including `0`, as `<path>: invalid process lock` and an unreadable lock as `<path>: <reason>`, as the endpoint specification now states, and the contract case `endpoint.process.rejects-a-malformed-lock` compares them; the Korean endpoint specification also said a lock could be removed while its process ran, which is corrected. Red: the tracked tests `TestEndpointRejectsAMalformedLock` and `a_malformed_process_lock_is_refused` failed against the unchanged hosts with `invalid process lock <path>` and `<path>: invalid process lock `abc`: invalid digit found in string`. Green: both tests and the endpoint tests of both hosts; macOS 26 arm64.

- [o] F21 — P1: End the persistent terminal service when the Tauri application quits after a close answer it did not expect. Found on 2026-10-04 when the Tauri check application (pid 98116, a build from before that day's changes) was quit with `host.quit`: its log ends with `sidecar @soksak/sidecar-vt-alacritty failed: unexpected close answer for state:files:prj-ocoeub` and `sidecar: close owner wait: timed out waiting on channel`, and the vt service (pid 71155) stayed running with parent 1 until it was ended by hand; the close answer of a files plugin state session reached the vt sidecar. Logs: `~/backup/soksak-check-logs/f21-tauri-quit-20261004.log`. The first step is to reproduce it with the current build. Completed on 2026-10-04: the cause is in both hosts. A window that closes sends `closed` to every running sidecar, and the stop at quit forgot every closing surface on the assumption that stopped sidecars do not answer; the persistent vt service still answers those closes ahead of its close-owner reply, so the host read the answer as `unexpected close answer`, ended the connection, never received the close-owner reply and never sent `shutdown`. The stop now forgets only the closing surfaces of standard input and output sidecars and keeps those of a persistent service until each answer arrives or its connection ends ([sidecars](spec/sidecars.md#messages)), contract case `sidecars-transport.stop.accepts-close-answers-sent-before-stop`. Red: `persistent_stop_accepts_the_answer_to_a_close_sent_before_the_stop` received `["hello", "open", "closed", "close-owner"]` without `shutdown`, and `TestPersistentStopAcceptsTheAnswerToACloseSentBeforeTheStop` received `hello,open,closed,close-owner`. Green: both pass 3 of 3 runs; `make host-contract-check` (Wails 344/344, Tauri 347/347 cases), `make host-parity-check docs-check parity-check`, and the Rust and Go format and clippy checks pass. Platform: macOS 26 arm64.

- [o] F35 — P1: Keep the window buttons centred in the first row after a text size change (verification W). Found on 2026-10-05 by F31: `error: verify: 1 fail — W 창 단추는 첫 행 가운데 (행 54.0px · 단추 14.0px · 위 13.0 아래 27.0)` failed `text size commands enlarge the pressed card or the frame and keep the plane in the window` on both hosts. Cause: the empty unified compact toolbar fixed the title bar at 40pt, AppKit centres the buttons in the title bar, and the page took its first row from the title bar and raised it with the frame factor, so at 1.5 the 54px row held buttons centred in 40pt (13 above, 27 below); the row also could not shrink, because it read the height back from the window. Red: `window_controls_test` and the Go and Rust `window_titlebar_test` did not build against the unchanged code (no `windowSetTitlebarHeight`, `ValidateTitlebarHeight`, `validate_titlebar_height`), and `packages/workbench/test/titlebar.test.mjs` failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `titlebar.js`. The row and the title bar must change in the same presented frame, so the title bar height joins the layout transaction that already presents native placement with the page frame. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (36fb65d2, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed) through F35.1 and F35.2; the W failure that the Wails log holds is from the earlier build of pid 89075.
  - [o] F35.1 — P1: Present the title bar height in the layout transaction of the frame that draws the new first row. Criterion, fixed before implementation and not lowered: in every presented frame of both hosts, the centre of the window buttons equals the centre of the first row within 0.5px, at every frame factor step up and down, and verification W passes at every step without an `expectError`. Design: the page computes the first-row height of the next draw and sends it with the native preparation (`prepare`); the host calls `-[NSWindow setTitlebarHeight:]` after it begins the window's CATransaction (`surfaceLayoutBegin` in `native/darwin/src/surface_layout.m`) and before the page draws, so the title bar change commits with the DOM frame; the separate page request after the draw is removed. A native test measures that the title bar change made inside an open transaction is not on screen before the commit and is after it, before the hosts depend on it. Native test measured on 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, at 7c66c527): `native/darwin/tests/window_titlebar_layout_test.m` records a titled full-size-content window without a toolbar through the non-activating window recording, opens the window's transaction with `surfaceLayoutBegin`, calls `windowSetTitlebarHeight` with 80pt and then with 40pt, runs the run loop for 12 display refreshes (92 to 111ms) before `surfaceLayoutCommit` and 12 after it, and measures the button rows in every recorded frame. In each of its runs, the model values change at the call (title bar 40 to 80pt, close button frame and layer frame y 13 to 33pt, button centre 20 to 40pt), while the close button's presentation layer stays at y 13pt until the commit; 9 to 12 recorded frames displayed between the call and the commit all show the buttons centred at the earlier 20pt (and 40pt on the way down), and the frames after the commit show the new centre from 8.6 to 16.9ms after the commit and keep it. The design is valid on the native side: a title bar height set in the open transaction reaches the screen with the commit and not before. The test is part of `make -C native/darwin test`, which passed; `make -C native/darwin repeat TEST=window_titlebar_layout_test COUNT=3` passed at a load average of 128 to 185. Implemented on 2026-10-05: every preparation (`syncSurfaces`) carries `titlebar`, the first-row height of the draw that follows it (`chromeRow` in `packages/workbench/frame-text.js`, which equals `--chrome-row` of `app.css`); both hosts check it before the transaction begins (`argument request.titlebar is missing`, `title bar height must be a finite number from 32 through 200 points`), set the title bar after `surfaceLayoutBegin` and before they place the surfaces, cancel the begun transaction when that step fails, and answer the window's `chrome`; verification W compares the first row with the `chrome` of the last presented preparation (`chrome.presented()` in `packages/workbench/host.js`). A frame factor change is drawn by a prepared layout: the setting no longer writes `--frame-text`, the plane's draw writes it, and the plane size of the preparation is measured at the new factor (`measureAt`); a window without a plane draws it with a preparation without surfaces. The `windowTitlebar` call, `packages/workbench/titlebar.js`, and the request after the draw are removed. In full screen `windowSetTitlebarHeight` leaves the height unchanged and succeeds, and the page prepares its row again when a `windowControls` answer (start document or resize) shows a title bar of another height. Red against the unchanged code (dd4e57b4): `pnpm -F @soksak/workbench test` failed 4 of 285 tests: `frame-text.test.mjs` with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `frame-text.js`, `plane-frame-text.test.mjs` with `undefined !== 54` (the layout receiver got no row), and `host-chrome.test.mjs` with `the page has no title bar request apart from the preparation`; Go `TestArgumentRefusalMessages` (`host call has no window, want argument request.titlebar is missing`) and `TestSyncRequestRejectsOtherTitlebarHeights` (`returned <nil> for title bar 31.99`); Rust `arguments_are_refused_with_the_shared_messages` (`{"settled":true,"surfaces":[]} was accepted`) and `sync_request_rejects_other_titlebar_heights` (`left: None`); the order tests `TestTitlebarIsSetInTheBegunLayoutBeforeTheSurfaces` and `the_titlebar_is_set_in_the_begun_layout_before_the_surfaces` did not build (`too many arguments in call to host.ApplyOrCancel`, `this function takes 4 arguments but 5 arguments were supplied`). Green, after the rebase onto 5c6d1799: the workbench tests pass 282 of 282; `make go-repeat PACKAGE=./packages/host/wailsv3/tests COUNT=1` and `make rust-repeat PACKAGE=soksak-host-tauriv2 COUNT=1` pass (the first Rust run failed `slow_sidecar_does_not_block_other_sends` with `stop() took 500.492ms, want < 200ms` at a load average of 324 and passed on the next run, classified as load); `make host-contract-check` (Wails 348 of 348, Tauri 352 of 352 cases), `make hosts-check platforms boundaries exposure-check docs-check parity-check`, `make -C native/darwin test`, and `pnpm test` pass, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 130 to 390. The native test commit before this change (dd4e57b4, rebased onto 5c6d1799 as 38192086) added a test file without updating the inventory count in `docs/operations/examples.md`; the first F35.1 change recorded the inventory count. Window start, found on 2026-10-05 by the coordinator's review of that change: the first draw of a page waits for no preparation, so a window created at a frame factor other than 1 drew its larger row under the 40pt title bar that the host set at creation. Done on 2026-10-05: before it answers the start document, each host sets the title bar to `round(max(40, 36 × textSize))` for the common `textSize` of the snapshot it sends (40 without it) and reads `controls` after that (`StartTitlebarHeight`, `start_titlebar_height`); a new window is still transparent then and becomes opaque with the presentation of that first draw. Setting the title bar at the start document rather than making the first draw a prepared layout follows from the page start contract: the first screen is drawn before the first await, because the load end that reveals a new window and the end of a reload do not wait for anything after it. `textSize` becomes common-only in both hosts (`<path>: textSize is common-only`, `textSize is common-only`) and in the page (`project settings: textSize is common-only`, `Text size is common-only`), so the host and the page take the row from the same value. A preparation whose surface step or image raster refresh fails now sets the previous title bar height again before it cancels, because cancelling commits the transaction. Library switch (`projects.onSwitch` `empty()`), verified from the code: the path cleared the plane and published without writing the factor, but it raises the layout epoch, which cancels the draw of a layout prepared before it, and that draw can be the one that writes a new factor, so the setting and the drawn factor stayed apart with no later draw; the switch is now a prepared layout (`frameLayout` in `frame-text.js`) whose preparation carries the row of the current factor and whose draw clears the plane and writes that factor. Red against 84c83984: the workbench tests `the frame text factor is common-only` (`Missing expected exception`) and `a frame layout prepares the row of its factor and writes the factor after clearing the plane` (`frameLayout is not a function`); Go `TestProjectTextSizeOverrideIsRejected` (`a project textSize write returned <nil>`) and Rust `a_project_text_size_override_is_rejected` (`left: None`); `TestStartTitlebarFollowsFrameFactor`, `the_start_titlebar_follows_the_frame_factor`, and the order tests with the title bar restore did not build (`undefined: host.StartTitlebarHeight`, `cannot use titlebar(nil, nil) … as func() error value`, `unresolved import start_titlebar_height`, `this function takes 5 arguments but 6 arguments were supplied`). In a visible window, it begins a start transaction as one preparation of the window with the host's next ticket, sets the height in it, and commits the transaction after the main web view's load ends and the next presentation update completes. A preparation of the new page in between extends the transaction and commits it. A failed height cancels the start transaction and fails the start. - [o] F43 — P1: Remove the ResizeObserver loop of the files tree section. Found on 2026-10-05 in the fifth full window run (`project windows persist files, inherit settings, and isolate native state` on Tauri, `removing a project ends the terminal sessions that its layout held` on Wails): the error frame ran only the observer of the vendor tree (`plugin-files/ui/vendor/trees.js:7930`) on its 188×498 container, and after it the frame changed `div.files-tree__message` `hidden`, the text and title of `span.files-tree__title`, the `disabled` of a section control and the child list of `ul.files-bookmarks`, the updates of the `files.tree` status callback in `ui/sections/tree.js`; the container then became 188×517 in the next frame. That conclusion was not shown by the record: `this frame changed` covered everything from the first callback to the next animation frame, including tasks that run after the observation round. Progress on 2026-10-05: the diagnostic recorder (`packages/workbench/resize-loop.js`) now divides the DOM changes of the error frame by callback slot. It takes the undelivered mutation records immediately before each callback, so the records of a slot are those of the previous callback and its microtask checkpoint, and it takes them again in the error event, which is dispatched after the round. The report lines are `before the round, undelivered at the first callback: …`, `in the round callback <n> ran <creator> … on <targets>, then changed …` for each callback, `after the round changed …` for the changes until the next animation frame, and `the next frame delivered …`. Red: `each DOM change is reported in the callback slot of the round it happened in, or after the round` (`packages/workbench/test/resize-loop.test.mjs`) failed on the earlier recorder, which reported the in-round changes in one line and no change after the round; Green: it passes. Next step: a window run that reads the new lines of the next loop error. Neither the targeted window run of 2026-10-05 nor the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (36fb65d2, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed) logged a ResizeObserver loop error, so the recorder has no occurrence to report yet; the item waits for the next occurrence. Occurred in the tenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (7eca547a, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 43 to 69; 336 of 344 checks passed) on Wails in `padding settings inset the terminal grid and show the terminal background`: the recorder reported `in the round callback 1 ran …/plugin-files/ui/vendor/trees.js:7930:86 … on div 188x498, then changed childList of div#plane.plane, attributes d of path#railPath, attributes hidden of div#focusMark.focus-mark`, after the round `childList of main.library-main`, and the next frame delivered `div 0x0`. The plane draw that shows the library ran inside the observation round. The explanation recorded first, that observers created before `observe.js` installs the recorder are not recorded and their changes went to callback 1, is wrong: no module that the page evaluates before `observe.js` creates a ResizeObserver, and every observer of the page (the plane view of `soksak`, surface composition, document and image regions, the vendor tree) constructs the `ResizeObserver` of the window when it is created at run time, so the recorder records it; the tree observer of this record was created at 166ms during the page start and was recorded. No ResizeObserver callback of core changes the document synchronously: the plane view's callback schedules a prepared layout, and the composition and region callbacks send host calls. The changes in callback 1 are those of `clear()` in `plane.js` (the cards of `#plane`, `d` of `railPath`, `hidden` of `focusMark`), which runs only in the draw of a prepared layout, here the switch to the library (`pageLayout.empty`), and `main.library-main` after the round is the library drawn after that layout. `drawPrepared` (`packages/workbench/layout-queue.js`) drew in the microtask checkpoint that resolved the preparation, and `surfaces.place` answers a request equal to the previous one with the earlier settled result, so the draw could run in any checkpoint, including the checkpoint of a ResizeObserver callback; which code resolved the preparation in the checkpoint of the tree callback is not determined from the code. Fixed on 2026-10-05: `drawPrepared` draws in the callback of the next animation frame after the preparation (`animationFrame(work)`), which runs before that frame's observation round, and a layout epoch change before that frame cancels the draw; [native surfaces](spec/native-surfaces.md) states the rule. A response that arrives between two rendering updates is drawn and presented in the same rendering update as before, and `presentSurfaces` was already sent after that animation frame, so the change adds no frame to such a layout; a preparation answered inside a rendering update is drawn one rendering update later, after its observation round. Red: `a prepared draw runs at the next animation frame when its preparation is answered inside an observation round` (`packages/workbench/test/layout-preparation.test.mjs`) failed with `the draw changed the tree container inside the observation round` (0 !== 498); Green: it passes with workbench 299 of 299. Acceptance is a window run without a ResizeObserver loop error whose alignment and divider-drag delay checks pass. Occurred again in the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05 (core a3498ed4, terminal service b9b46c4, terminal plugin dfd2858, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 26 to 47; 339 of 344 checks passed) on Tauri in `native clicks reach every chrome icon at wide window sizes`, twice: in the round callback 1 of the files tree observer, the changes are the library screen of a project window (`data-screen` of `body`, the project and space bars, the chrome buttons and the library grid), and the next frame delivered the terminal view and the tree container at 0x0. The plane draw now waits for its animation frame, but the screen switch to the library still runs inside the round, so the code that starts it in that checkpoint is still to be found. Changed on 2026-10-05: the switch to the library now shows the library screen in the same prepared draw that empties the plane (`frameLayout` takes `show`, `createPageLayout().empty(show)`, `projects.js` `emptyToLibrary`), which runs at the animation frame before the observation round, so the plane clear and the library screen appear in one frame and the screen switch no longer runs at a later reaction. Which code started the switch inside the tree observer's callback slot is not yet measured; the diagnostic recorder now reports each write of a `body` dataset attribute inside a callback slot with the stack of the code that wrote it. Red (against the earlier code): `browsing shows the library in the draw that empties the plane, not where a later host reply resolves` (`the library screen was not drawn by the draw that empties the plane`) and `a body dataset write inside a callback slot is reported with the stack of the code that wrote it`; Green: both pass with the 302 workbench tests. Its acceptance is a full window run without the loop line, or the stack of the next occurrence. Accepted in the thirteenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (eb707869, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 58 to 93; 334 of 344 checks passed): neither application log has a ResizeObserver loop line, as in the twelfth run.
