A check leaves no state that changes another check; the cause of the refusal (F37) and the way an open press is ended after it are both still to be decided from the measured mask and frontmost application. Decided on 2026-10-05 from the measured mask 0x1 while another application was frontmost: a person held the left button, so the harness waits for the hardware release before it ends the press. Progress on 2026-10-05: both hosts declare `host.buttons` `{mask}` ([exposure](spec/exposure.md#host-entries), contract case `exposure.host-buttons.notifies-mask-change`). `native/darwin/src/mouse_buttons.m` reads `NSEvent.pressedMouseButtons` at every mouse button press and release that AppKit delivers to the application (local event monitor) or to another application (global event monitor), and the hosts notify watchers when the mask changes. `releasePresses` in `e2e/app.mjs` waits through `status.watch` until `host.buttons` reports mask 0 and then requires the release to be delivered; the refused check still fails with its 1007. Red: `a refused release keeps the press open until the held button is released` (`e2e/test/pointer-presses.test.mjs`) failed with `the synthetic left press at 10,20 in main stayed open: AppKit reports NSEvent.pressedMouseButtons mask 0x1 …`; `TestExposureListAppendsHostEntries` and `TestExposureListHostEntriesAreSortedAndDescribed` (Go) and `host_entries_are_appended_as_registered` (Rust) failed without `host.buttons`; `TestButtonsNotifyEachMaskChange` (Go), `buttons_notify_each_mask_change` (Rust) and `mouse_buttons_test` (native) did not build without the new interface. Green: all pass, with the Go and Rust host suites and `make host-contract-check`. `mouse_buttons_test` checks the local monitor with events posted to the application queue; the global monitor receives only a person's button or input posted to the window server, so its delivery while the application is inactive is observed only in a window run. Retry condition: a window run in which a person presses a button during a check; the acceptance is that no later check fails with 1008. The ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (36fb65d2, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed) had no refused press and no 1008, so the release wait was not exercised. In the thirteenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (eb707869, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 58 to 93; 334 of 344 checks passed) a person used Safari during the run: Wails refused one `input.pointer` with `mask 0x1 while com.apple.Safari (pid 28753) is frontmost`, and no later check failed with 1008; the log does not show whether the refused event was the press or the release, so the release wait is still not observed. Done on 2026-10-07 by its retry condition: in the completion window run (core 05676e63, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, 342 of 354 checks passed) and its reruns a person pressed a button in another application during three checks, and `input.pointer` refused `input.pointer down of the left button at 1406,19.5 in main` (Wails), `… at 214,124 in main` (Tauri) and `… at 2266,19.5 in main` (Tauri) with `mask 0x1`; no later check failed with 1008. All three refusals were presses, so no press stayed open and the release wait did not run; a refused release prints `released open press:` when it does. The other failures of that run were a person activating the check applications (eight Tauri checks and one Wails check, `tested host … is frontmost` and `host.active` true) and the alignment check at p90 55.9 ms and 56.4 ms against 50 ms at load average 7 to 18, classified as load; the seven affected files pass when run again.
  - [o] F46.1 — P1: Record which synthetic event a held button refused and that the cleanup ended the open press. Found on 2026-10-07: the refusals of the thirteenth full window run and of the F84.5 repeat on Wails (`mask 0x1 while com.stablyai.orca (pid 98677) is frontmost`) say `the synthetic press or release was not delivered`, and the cleanup prints nothing when it ends a press, so neither run shows whether the release wait ran. A refused `input.pointer` error of the harness names its phase, button, position and window, and `releasePresses` reports each press it ended with the time it waited for `host.buttons` mask 0 as a `released open press:` diagnostic. Done on 2026-10-07 in `Session.pointer` and `releasePresses` of `packages/window-check/app.mjs`; the session cleanup prints each returned line with `t.diagnostic`. Red: `a refused release keeps the press open until the held button is released` (`packages/window-check/test/pointer-presses.test.mjs`) failed because the error was only the host's text; Green: the harness tests pass 52 of 52, and `space-apps.test.mjs` passes on each host with native clicks (macOS 26.6.2 arm64). F46 keeps its retry condition, and a window run now shows whether the release wait ran.
- [o] F47 — P1: Write each host failure to the application log as an error line. Found on 2026-10-05 in the logs of the seventh full window run (a232bf46, macOS 26.6.2 arm64): only page lines take the `error: ` form, and the hosts write failures without it, for example `exposure settled failed: surface tab-… is not mounted` (Wails 4, Tauri 8), `host presentSurfaces failed while advancing the layout queue: …` and `sidecar: writer shutdown failed: Socket is not connected (os error 57)`, so a window check does not see them, although a window check fails on every application error logged while it runs. Each host log site that states a failure is classified as an error, which takes the `error: <where>: <text>` form in both hosts with the same text, or as an observation whose wording states the expected state, with a test of the line form at each owning host and a contract case for the shared form. Progress on 2026-10-05: two of the three examples were page lines, not host lines: the workbench sent `exposure settled failed: …`, `exposure: …` and `host <phase> failed while advancing the layout queue: …` through `report` without `error: `; `connectExposure` and `revisitRegistrations` now take the page's `report`, and the layout queue failure takes `errorLine`. [Hosts](spec/hosts.md#application-log) states that a host error line has the page form `error: <where>: <text>`, written through `LogError` (Go), `log_error` (Rust) and `sp_log_error` (native library), and that a host line without `error: ` is an observation that states the expected state; contract case `log.error.line-form`. Classification of the host, native and page sites: errors — every failed native call, event emit, endpoint read, write, close and encode, start document and installed module read, image reply, response, recovery and presentation failure (`error: image present: …`), sidecar write, close, kill, wait, read, protocol failure and restart failure, WebKit child record and kill failure, performance trace, menu command, window title bar, window prepare and close, surface layout cancel, notification and modal failure, Wails framework errors (`ErrorHandler`), and the native capture, surface settle, webview input and surface background failures; a late result that carries a failure after its request ended is now written as an error, because no request reports it; fatal exits after the log is open (`quit request`, `dock menu`, `main webview identity`, `file drop`, `window reveal`) stay fatal and write the error line first. Observations, worded as the expected state: `exposure reply … of removed surface … arrived after its request ended`, `<result> arrived after its request ended` for a completion whose caller already returned (it was `had no pending receiver`), the stale image frame line, `native event … of closed surface … arrived after the surface closed` (Wails), the buffered sidecar replies and closes, `sidecar <name>: connection lost; restarted`, the discarded disconnected connection, the service output after the ready bound, `sidecar <name>: the connection closed before its writer shut down` for ENOTCONN only (the reader reports the lost connection; another shutdown error is an error), the WebKit child reap decisions, the WebKit baseline count, and the native capture trace lines. `exposure settled failed: surface … is not mounted` is an error: every core command waits in `drawn` (`packages/workbench/index.html`) for each slot that names a native surface, and a slot whose surface was disposed after the last draw makes the wait throw, so the command answers without its settled wait; the sequence that leaves such a slot is F50. Native findings fixed in the same change: `surface_layout.m` wrote a literal `\n` instead of a line end, which joined the next log line to it, and the Tauri document close and background paths returned without a line when `platform::current()` failed. Red: `TestLogErrorWritesAnErrorLineToTheApplicationLog` and `log_error_writes_an_error_line_to_the_application_log` did not compile against the unchanged hosts (`undefined: host.LogError`, `unresolved import soksak_host_tauriv2::application_log::log_error`), native `application_log_test` did not compile (`'application_log.h' file not found`), `TestPresentationOutcomeNamesTheCurrentFrameOfAFailure` and `presentation_outcome_names_the_current_frame_of_a_failure` failed with `image present on main thread error: …`, and the workbench tests `a failed settling wait of a core command and a refused registration are error lines` and the layout queue assertion in `native preparation cannot present before DOM drawing and presents each ticket once` failed with the lines without `error: `. Green on macOS 26.6.2 arm64: the same tests pass; `make go-repeat PACKAGE=./packages/host/wailsv3/tests COUNT=1`, `make rust-repeat PACKAGE=soksak-host-tauriv2 COUNT=1`, `make host-contract-check` (353 cases), `make hosts-check boundaries exposure-check docs-check`, the Rust clippy and format checks, and the affected native tests pass. Retry condition for acceptance: a window run whose check failures include host error lines. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (36fb65d2, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped` failed on Tauri because of the host error line `error: image presentation timeout: …`, so host errors now fail window checks; the difference from Wails, which writes no such line, is F56.
- [o] F48 — P1: Find why a Tauri `status.get host.windows` failed with `runtime error: failed to receive message from webview`. Found on 2026-10-05 in the targeted window run (91ba4a41, load average 49 to 98): `tauriv2: a newly split terminal presents its first native raster` failed after 10.6s with that error. `tauri::Error::FailedToReceiveMessage` comes from `rx.recv()` after `run_on_main_thread` (tauri 2.11.5 `src/lib.rs:1091`) or from tauri-runtime-wry (`src/lib.rs:202`, `2084`), which means the closure that should answer was dropped without sending, not that the answer was slow. Which main-thread task was dropped and why is not yet known. Cause found on 2026-10-05 by reading the sources (tauri, tauri-runtime and tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.1 as `Cargo.lock` pins them; the versions above were wrong): the text is `tauri_runtime::Error::FailedToReceiveMessage` (tauri-runtime `src/lib.rs:151`) from the `getter!` macro (tauri-runtime-wry `src/lib.rs:196-202`) of `window.title()` or `window.is_focused()` in `windows::list` (`packages/host/tauriv2/src/windows.rs:198-251`). That list reads each window's `closing` flag on the endpoint thread and then queries the window in separate main-thread round trips; when the main thread processes the window's close in between, our close listener sets `closing` and `on_window_close` sets the window's `inner` to `None` (tauri-runtime-wry `src/lib.rs:4351-4387`), and `handle_user_message` drops the reply channel of a window without `inner` without answering (`src/lib.rs:3214-3233`, `3574-3576`). The failing request was the first `host.windows` read of `fresh()` (e2e/app.mjs:581) right after it closed the project window that the previous library check left open (F49). Correction: read the flag and query every window in one main-thread step, so no close can come between them; `send_user_message` handles a window message at once on the main thread (`src/lib.rs:263-273`). Implemented on 2026-10-05: `windows::list` passes every registered window to `list_entries` (`packages/host/tauriv2/src/windows.rs`), which builds all entries in one main-thread step through `exposure::app_on_main`; `windows_changed` and `sidecars_changed` read the list through the same function. A window getter called on the main thread is handled at once and does not wait (tauri-runtime-wry `send_user_message`, `src/lib.rs:263-273`); it cannot deadlock on the runtime's window store, because `handle_user_message` runs `Message::Task` without a borrow (`src/lib.rs:3182`) and releases its borrow of the store before it answers a window message (`src/lib.rs:3214-3226`). The other host statuses do not read the `closing` flag: `host.window` reads one window, and `host.screens`, `host.dock` and `host.menu` read the application. Wails needs no change: `hostBackend.Windows` (`packages/host/wailsv3/src/exposure.go`) reads the title from host state, and `WebviewWindow.IsFocused` (wails v3.0.0-beta.27 `pkg/application/webview_window.go:781-786`) reads the native window on the main thread, where `destroy` has already set it to nil after closing it (`webview_window_darwin.go:1889-1901`), so a close during the list yields `false`, not an error. Red (macOS 26, worktree at 48ba7fc8 with `list_entries` running the entries on the calling thread as before, load 238): the new contract case `exposure.windows.listed-in-one-main-thread-step`, test `a_close_during_the_list_does_not_fail_the_list` in `packages/host/tauriv2/tests/exposure_test.rs`, which queues a close on a test main thread at the moment the list reads the flag, failed with `left: Err("runtime error: failed to receive message from webview")`, `right: Ok([main, w2])`. Green: the same test passes, and `make rust-repeat PACKAGE=soksak-host-tauriv2 COUNT=1` passes every Tauri host test, including `a_closing_window_is_left_out_without_querying_it` and `a_failed_query_of_an_open_window_is_reported`; `make host-contract-check` passes 353 cases. An earlier run of that check failed the unchanged `persistent_transport_replaces_endpoint_left_by_a_dead_service` in the default configuration with `the service did not print its endpoint within 30s` at load 402 while it passed in the diagnostics configuration; `make rust-repeat TEST=persistent_transport_replaces_endpoint_left_by_a_dead_service COUNT=3` passed 3 of 3 at load 324, so the failure is classified as load. Finding outside this correction: `host.window` (`window_status`) and the commands that call `native_owner_on_main` read the native window handle in one main-thread step and use it in a later one, so a close between the steps can pass a closed window's pointer to native code; whether the window object is freed before `Destroyed` is not yet verified, and the finding needs its own item. Acceptance: a window run in which `fresh()` closes windows without this error. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (36fb65d2, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): no `failed to receive message` line and no failure of `fresh()`.
- [o] F49 — P1: Decide and implement what happens to an open project window when its project is removed from the library. Found on 2026-10-05 while finding the cause of F48: `library names a missing project folder and removes the project` (e2e/library.test.mjs) opens the project in its own window, removes the project with `core.library.remove`, and its cleanup closes only projects still in `core.projects`, so the window of the removed project stays open and the next check closes it. [projects](spec/projects.md) says the removal deletes the record and its spaces like closing a project tab, but not what happens to a window that shows that project. Decided and implemented on 2026-10-05 ([projects](spec/projects.md#settings)): closing a window's last project tab releases the window and shows the library in the same OS window (`projects.close`, host `projectRelease`), so a removal does the same in the window that shows the project; the window stays open as a window without a project and is not closed. That window read the removal through `readProjects` and showed the library, but kept the surface modules of the removed project's tabs, so the host kept their terminal sessions, and it did not open its next project tab. `readProjects` now ends every removed project in each window: it disposes the surface modules of its tabs, ends their sidecar sessions, and the change notification opens the window's first remaining project. Red: `projects-switch.test.mjs` `a project removed from the registry by another window ends in the window that shows it as closing its tab does` failed on the unchanged module with `the window did not open its next project as closing the project tab does` (actual `undefined`, expected `prj-next`); Green: it passes with the workbench suite (282 tests). The library check now waits on `host.windows` until the project window shows no project, on `core.screen` for the library, and on `host.window` until the native surfaces of the removed project's terminals are gone, then closes the window it opened. Acceptance: that library window check on both hosts. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (36fb65d2, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): `the library names a missing project folder and removes the project` passed on both hosts.
- [o] F50 — P1: Find why the settled wait of a core command finds a slot whose native surface is not mounted. Found on 2026-10-05 in F47: the seventh full window run logged `exposure settled failed: surface tab-… is not mounted` four times on Wails and eight times on Tauri. `drawn` in `packages/workbench/index.html` waits for the current draw and then for the composition of every slot with `data-native-surface-id`; `waitSurfaceCompositionDeclared` throws when the slot names a surface that `disposeSurface` already removed, which happens when a tab close or a project switch disposes a surface after the last draw and before the next one. Whether a command can overlap such a removal, which makes the removed surface a declared state that the wait skips, or whether a slot outlives its surface in one command, which is a defect of the draw order, is decided from the run evidence with a workbench test that reproduces the sequence. Cause found on 2026-10-05 from the logs of the seventh full run and the targeted run that followed (e2e-full7 and e2e-target1, a232bf46 and 91ba4a41, macOS 26.6.2 arm64): each line is written just before the page reload of the next check's `fresh()`, and in the terminal checks the check before it ends with `closeTerminalTabs`, which runs `core.tab.close` for every terminal tab one after another (Wails lines 22662 and 22742 follow `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped …` and `a terminal split from a terminal starts in the directory …`; Tauri lines 537, 538 and 541 and target1 lines 831 and 834 follow the same checks). Two defects let a settled wait read a slot list older than a disposal. First, the `core.tab.close` handler (`core-exposure.js`) called `closeTabById(tab)` without returning its promise, so the command ran its settled wait and answered while `closeTab` was still disposing the surface; `closeTab` disposes the surface first and only then removes the tab and schedules the layout without its slot, so the next `core.tab.close` of the check, or the next check, ran its wait while the disposed surface still had its slot. ac806640 made `closeTab` asynchronous for this wait but did not change the handler. Second, `drawn` (`index.html`) awaited the `drawing` promise once; a layout that a newer layout replaces resolves `{status: "superseded"}` without a draw, so a wait that began before the next tab close scheduled its layout ended before the draw that removes the slot and read the slots of the earlier draw; `layout: <n> waiting layouts were replaced by newer layouts before presentation` precedes most of the lines. Correction: `core.tab.close` awaits `closeTabById`, and `drawn` waits through `wait()` of the layout queue, which waits for the newest layout and waits again while a newer one was scheduled, and fails with the failure of the newest layout; [exposure](spec/exposure.md#registration) states the rule. The other lines (Wails 21081 and 21629, Tauri 498, 507, 517, 743 and 744, target1 800, 808 and 1065) also stand before the reload of a `fresh()` and after a replaced layout, but the run had no performance trace, so the logs do not name their command; the corrected wait covers every removal that schedules a layout. A disposal that leaves a slot without a scheduled layout remains only inside `closeTab` between the end of `disposeSurface` and its `settle()`, which run in one microtask checkpoint, so a wait cannot read the slots between them unless the same task resolves the layout that the wait awaits. Red: `core.tab.close answers after the tab close and its draw` (`test/tab-close-settled.test.mjs`) recorded `['close tab-a', 'settled']` before the close finished, and `the wait for the drawn layout continues through a layout that a newer layout replaces` read `["tab-a","tab-b"]` instead of `[]`, and `the wait for the drawn layout fails with the failure of the newest layout` failed with the error of the replaced layout. Green: the same tests and `pnpm -F @soksak/workbench test` pass. Acceptance: a window run without `exposure settled failed: surface … is not mounted`. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (36fb65d2, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): neither application log has a `is not mounted` line.
- [o] F51 — P1: Use a native window handle only in the main-thread step that reads it. Found on 2026-10-05 while fixing F48: `host.window` (`window_status` in `packages/host/tauriv2/src/exposure.rs`) and the commands that call `native_owner_on_main` (`surfaces.rs` lines 212, 370, 547, 740; `exposure.rs` lines 1247, 1366, 1543, 1582, 1656) read the native window handle in one main-thread step and pass it to native code in a later one, so a close between the steps can pass the handle of a closed window to native code such as `sp_window_facts`. Measured on 2026-10-05 from the sources (tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.1 and tao at rev 1a047e2, as `Cargo.lock` pins them): when no listener prevents a close, `on_close_requested` calls `on_window_close` in the same main-thread pass, and `on_window_close` sets the window's `inner` to `None`, which drops the last `Arc` of the tao window. `UnownedWindow::drop` then sends `close` to the NSWindow at once (`close_async` runs inline on the main thread), `windowWillClose:` removes the delegate and queues `Destroyed`, and the drop releases the two strong references that tao holds (`UnownedWindow.ns_window` and the copy in the delegate state; the window has `releasedWhenClosed` off). The NSWindow is therefore closed, and freed unless another owner retains it, before `Destroyed` is delivered, so a handle read before the close names a closed and possibly freed object. Progress on 2026-10-05: every Tauri request that uses the native window reads it in the main-thread step that passes it to native code (`windows::use_owner` through `with_native_owner`): `host.window`, `host.window.fullscreen`, `host.window.move`, `host.hit`, `input.pointer` (activation, delivery and surface press), `input.key`, the surface press watch, and the title bar, begin, commit and cancel steps of the surface layout; the initial title bar reads the handle in its own main-thread task. A window whose close was accepted, or whose registration `Destroyed` removed, is closed at that step: native code does not receive it, the request fails with 1003 `window "<name>" does not exist`, a `host.window` change of it notifies nothing, and a layout cancel of it has nothing to cancel because `Destroyed` cancels its layout. The surface press of `input.pointer` ran AppKit hit testing on the endpoint thread; it now runs in the main-thread step. The Tauri unknown-window message now quotes the name as Wails does. Wails already read `NativeWindow()` in the step that uses it, where Wails' destroy has set it to nil, but passed that nil to native code; through `UseNativeWindow` it now answers the same 1003. Red: with the handle read and used in two steps, the new Rust case `a_close_after_the_handle_read_does_not_reach_native_code` failed with `left: Err(Failed("native code messaged the closed window 0x5157")) right: Ok("facts of 0x5157")`; the new Go case `TestACloseBeforeTheNativeStepDoesNotReachNativeCode`, with the nil passed to native code, failed with `a window closed before the step: <nil>`. Green: both pass under the new contract case `window-close.native-window.used-in-reading-step`; the Tauri and Wails host suites, `make host-contract-check` (359 cases), `hosts-check`, `boundaries`, `docs-check`, `parity-check`, `exposure-check` and `pnpm test` pass on macOS 26.6.2 arm64 at load average 50 to 100. Open: the window checks against rebuilt hosts. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (36fb65d2, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): every window close and reload check passed on both hosts.
- [o] F52 — P1: Build both hosts for Windows in the checks and make every unsupported operation return its error. Found on 2026-10-05 while F46 was implemented: `GOOS=windows go vet ./src/platform/windows/` in `packages/host/wailsv3` fails with `unsupported.go:218:14: undefined: missing` on main, because `CreateSurface` calls a `missing` helper that does not exist since 7e6b17d4. `make platforms` and `make hosts-check` check only the file layout, so no check builds the Windows hosts. The same file has operations that return without an error (`CloseSurface`, `SetSurfaceBounds`, `SurfaceFrame`), although [hosts](spec/hosts.md#windows-state) says that every operation outside directory identity returns `<operation> is not implemented on windows`. The Rust host is to be checked the same way; the `aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm` and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm` targets are installed. Found on 2026-10-05 while F52 was audited, before its fix: the Windows builds also fail outside the Windows files. Go `src/sidecars.go:824` sets `syscall.SysProcAttr.Setsid`, and Rust `src/application_log.rs` uses `std::os::unix::fs` modes, so both are platform work in shared files and move into platform operations under `platform/<os>/`. The Go `Platform` rule that functions without an error take only handles from error-returning constructors is broken by `ConfigureMainWindow`, `PreferredLanguage`, `MainWindow` and `ServiceProcessExists`, which return errors in Rust and are to return them in Go. `cargo check --target aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm` needs a Windows C compiler (`aarch64-w64-mingw32-clang`) for `ring`, which this machine does not have. Progress on 2026-10-05: `make windows-build-check` vets the Wails host source (`./src/...`) for `windows/arm64` in the default and the `diagnostics` build, and `make hosts-check` runs it; the host tests are not compiled for Windows, because they run only on macOS ([host contract](spec/host-contract.md#check)) and use POSIX calls such as `syscall.Mkfifo`. Every operation of `platform/windows/unsupported.*` returns `<operation> is not implemented on windows` or, without an error result in Go, panics with that error through `unreachable`; the Go `missing` and `unreachableError` helpers that did not exist are removed, and the operation names of both hosts are the same. Starting a process in a new session is the platform operation `NewSession` (Go) that Darwin implements with `Setsid` and Windows refuses. The Rust log files are created through `create_private_directories` and the new `append_private_file`, so `application_log.rs` uses no `std::os::unix`. `ConfigureMainWindow`, `PreferredLanguage`, `MainWindow` and `ServiceProcessExists` return errors in Go, and their callers report them: a failed theme answers the page with the error, a failed main window configuration ends the application through `fatalError`, and a menu command without the main window logs the error. The Rust initial menu language took the default language when the system language could not be read (`unwrap_or_default`); in both hosts that failure now fails startup. With errors from `ServiceProcessExists`, the Go host stopped treating a refused signal check (EPERM) as an existing process, and Rust already failed on it; both hosts now treat EPERM as an existing process, because the refusal shows that the process exists (contract case `sidecars-transport.endpoint.foreign-service-process-exists`). Red: on main, `make windows-build-check` failed with `unsupported.go:218:14: undefined: missing` and `unsupported.go:374:13: undefined: unreachableError`, and after the Windows-file fixes with `sidecars.go:824:42: unknown field Setsid`; `scripts/test/windows-build-check.test.mjs` failed on the unchanged Go host with the same errors; the new foreign-process cases failed with `cannot inspect service process 1: operation not permitted` (Go, after the signature change) and `Operation not permitted (os error 1)` (Rust). Green: the same test and cases pass; the Wails and Tauri host suites pass on macOS 26.6.2 arm64. For diagnosis only, `cargo check -p soksak-host-tauriv2 --target aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm` with zig as the C compiler (`CRATE_CC_NO_DEFAULTS=1`) failed on the unchanged `application_log.rs` with `cannot find unix in os` and passes after the change in the default and `diagnostics` builds; this is not evidence of the check. Open: `make windows-build-check-rust` fails with `FAIL: windows-build-check-rust requires the Windows C compiler aarch64-w64-mingw32-clang, which is not installed` until that compiler is installed, which is a decision of the user; it then runs in `make hosts-check`. Completed on 2026-10-05: llvm-mingw 20260922 (clang 23.1.2, sha256 `52e5f5a7b131021d0c39a37a38fa380a1da7885cd04bd61afd0cd4ecfb8bc1f3`) is installed in `~/.local/opt/llvm-mingw` with the user's approval, the Makefile declares it as `LLVM_MINGW` and passes its compiler and archiver to `cc` through `CC_aarch64_pc_windows_gnullvm` and `AR_aarch64_pc_windows_gnullvm`, and `make hosts-check` runs `windows-build-check-rust`. - [o] F56 — P1: Make one presentation timeout write the same lines in both hosts. Found on 2026-10-05 in the ninth full window run (36fb65d2): an image presentation timeout writes `error: image presentation timeout: pending surface=…` on Tauri and no host line on Wails, while both hosts and the page write `host presentSurfaces failed …`, `exposure settled failed …` and `page: surface presentation failed …` for the same failure, so `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped` failed only on Tauri. A failure that a requester receives is reported by that requester, and a host writes an error line only for a failure that no request reports; which of these lines remain is to be decided by that rule. Progress on 2026-10-05: the three lines that both hosts were said to write are page lines: `host presentSurfaces failed while advancing the layout queue: …` from the continuation of the layout transaction order in `packages/workbench/host.js`, `page: surface presentation failed: …` from the layout queue's `failed` in `packages/workbench/index.html`, and `exposure settled failed: …` from the settled wait of the core command. By the rule one line remains, the page display `error: page: surface presentation failed: <text>`, because the layout queue receives the failure as the answer of its `place` request and shows it: the Tauri `Images::wait_current` no longer writes `image presentation timeout` (its callers answer the preparation or presentation request with the pending regions, and Wails wrote no line), the transaction order continues after a failed step without a line (the `place` caller receives every failure of a step), and the layout queue's `wait()` answers `false` for a failed newest layout instead of throwing its failure again, so the settled wait ends without reading slots; a failure of the settled wait itself, such as `surface <id> is not mounted`, is still written as `exposure settled failed: …`. [Hosts](spec/hosts.md#application-log) and [exposure](spec/exposure.md#registration) state the application of the rule, contract case `images.wait.timeout-writes-no-log-line`, and `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped` declares only `/^error: page: surface presentation failed: the current image raster did not present within /`. Red: `presentation_wait_timeout_returns_its_failure_and_writes_no_log_line` failed with `a presentation timeout wrote host lines: ["… application log: com.soksak.test pid …", "error: image presentation timeout: pending surface=tab-1 name=view generation=1 raster=1 sequence=0 configured=true presentedRaster=0 presentedSequence=0 handle=100"]`; `TestPresentationWaitTimeoutReturnsItsFailureAndWritesNoLogLine` passed against the unchanged Wails host; the workbench test `one presentation timeout writes one page error line` failed with the three lines `error: host presentSurfaces failed while advancing the layout queue: …`, `error: page: surface presentation failed: …` and `error: exposure settled failed: …`; `native preparation cannot present before DOM drawing and presents each ticket once` failed with `error: host syncSurfaces failed while advancing the layout queue: injected syncSurfaces failure`, and the two layout queue tests failed with the rejection `current image raster did not present`. Green on macOS 26.6.2 arm64: the same tests pass. Retry condition for acceptance: a window run in which the check passes on both hosts with the one declared line. Accepted in the tenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (7eca547a, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 43 to 69; 336 of 344 checks passed): `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped` passed on both hosts with its one declared line.

- [o] F58 — P2: Move the layout wiring of `packages/workbench/index.html` into a module that the tests import. Found on 2026-10-05 in the review of F56 and F57: `presentation-failure-lines.test.mjs` and `layout-failure-lines.test.mjs` rebuild a copy of the inline wiring of `index.html` (the layout queue, `showError`, the `unhandledrejection` report and `presented()`), so they verify the copy and not the page; a test exercises a module through its exports, and the wiring is to move into an exported module that `index.html` and both tests use. - [o] F59 — P2: Make both hosts create owner-only files the same way on Windows. Found on 2026-10-05 in F52: the Rust host creates its private log file and directories through platform operations that return `not implemented on windows`, while the Go host's `OpenLog` and the `os.Chmod` in `sidecars.go` use portable `os` permission modes that compile on Windows without giving owner-only access. Startup fails earlier on Windows (F54), so the difference is not reached today; the Go creation of private files is to move into the same platform operations. Resolved on 2026-10-05: both hosts create owner-only files and directories only through the platform operations `CreatePrivateDirectories`, `AppendPrivateFile`, `CreatePrivateFile`, `WritePrivateFile`, `SecureServiceDirectory` and `PrivateDirectory` in Go and `create_private_directories`, `append_private_file`, `create_private_file`, `write_private_file`, `secure_service_directory` and the diagnostic `private_directory` in Rust, which `platform/darwin/private_files.*` implements with modes 0700 and 0600; `CreatePrivateFile` and `create_private_file` are new and create a file that must not exist; `WritePrivateFile` and `write_private_file` are new and replace the contents of a file. Windows returns `private directory creation`, `private file creation`, `new private file creation`, `private file writing`, `persistent sidecar service directory` and `private directory` with `is not implemented on windows` in both hosts. The Go sites that now use them are the application and service logs, the configuration and settings directories, the process lock, the clipboard image and its directory, the service directory, the performance switch, service flags, output and logs directory, the WebKit child record, and the diagnostic recording, still-capture and fixture directories. The Rust host created the process lock (0644), the services, clipboard, settings, endpoint record and performance logs directories, the performance switch, service flags and output, the WebKit child record and the diagnostic fixture settings with the umask mode; it now uses the same operations, so these have the Go modes 0700 and 0600. Files of the temporary-file helpers (Go `os.CreateTemp`, Rust `tempfile`) keep the mode 0600 that the helpers set. [Hosts](spec/hosts.md#platform-interface) lists the operations. Red: the new Go cases failed to compile with `Platform has no field or method CreatePrivateDirectories` (and `AppendPrivateFile`, `CreatePrivateFile`), the new Rust cases with `no method named create_private_file`, and the Rust case `the_process_lock_is_owner_only` failed with `left: 420, right: 384` (mode 0644, want 0600); the Go process lock already had mode 0600. The new Rust cases `enable_creates_owner_only_files` and `the_webkit_child_record_is_owner_only` failed with `…/performance has mode 644` and `record has mode 644`. Green: the contract cases `platform.private.creates-owner-only-directories`, `platform.private.appends-owner-only-file`, `platform.private.creates-new-owner-only-file`, `platform.private.writes-owner-only-file`, `performance.trace.owner-only-files`, `webkit-children.record.owner-only` and `endpoint.process.lock-mode-0600` pass in both hosts on macOS 26.6.2 arm64, and `make windows-build-check` compiles the Go Windows implementation in the default and diagnostics builds. The Windows errors are checked only by that compilation, because the host tests run only on macOS. Accepted in the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05 (core a3498ed4, terminal service b9b46c4, terminal plugin dfd2858, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 26 to 47; 339 of 344 checks passed): every check passed on both hosts with the owner-only files.
- [o] F60 — P1: Find why Tauri presents an image for a surface it does not find. Found in the tenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (7eca547a): `both hosts answer the same page the same way` failed with the Tauri host line `error: image present: surface=tab-wlo6p3 name=view generation=256 raster=5 sequence=4 token=1451 reason=notFound current none`, which F47 made visible; Wails wrote no such line. Progress on 2026-10-05: `notFound` names the transfer image, not the surface: the native presentation (`sp_region_present` in `native/darwin/src/image_region.m`) found no IOSurface for the frame's token. Both hosts handle the case with the same code (`HandleEnvelope` in `packages/host/wailsv3/src/images.go`, `handle_envelope_with_recovery` in `packages/host/tauriv2/src/images.rs`) under the existing contract cases `images.present.failure-line-names-the-current-frame` and `images.present.rejects-frame-detached-during-main-thread`; Wails did not meet the timing in this run. The main-thread step checks the frame against the region state before it presents, so the region was attached when the IOSurface was missing, and `current none` shows that its state was removed right after that step. The check had started with `fresh` (`e2e/app.mjs`), which resizes the window, which configures a new raster, and runs `diagnostics.fixture`, which closes the previous check's project and disposes the module of its terminal tab `tab-wlo6p3`; that tab appears in no other line of the Tauri log. The terminal module's `dispose` sends the sidecar `close`, which ends the session and releases its transfer images, and then disposes its composition, which detaches the region; the shell module does the same. A frame that the supplier sent before `close` therefore reached a region that was still attached with a released transfer image. The error line is correct, and the cause is the order: the workbench now detaches the regions of a module's compositions before it calls the module's `dispose` (`disposeModule` in `packages/workbench/surface-modules.js`, [plugins](spec/plugins.md#surface-module-ownership)), so such a frame is answered `stale` for a detached region. No host change is needed, so the hosts have no Red test. Red: `removing a surface detaches its regions before the module ends its sidecar session` (`packages/workbench/test/surface-dispose-order.test.mjs`) failed with the order `["session close", "imageDetach view"]` against the expected `["imageDetach view", "session close"]`; Green: it passes, and the 297 workbench tests pass. Acceptance: a full window run whose application logs have no `reason=notFound` line. Accepted in the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05 (core a3498ed4, terminal service b9b46c4, terminal plugin dfd2858, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 26 to 47; 339 of 344 checks passed): neither application log has a `reason=notFound` line.
- [o] F61 — P1: Find why a Tauri terminal close answered before its PTY child was reaped. Found in the tenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (7eca547a): `closing terminal tabs reaps every PTY child without killing the shared service` failed on Tauri with `normal terminal close must reap every PTY child before the close answer` and child 12783 still present; the same check passed in the earlier runs. Cause found on 2026-10-05: the terminal service answers `closed` before its surface actor closes the session. The check waits until `host.sidecars` no longer lists the closed surfaces; both hosts remove a surface from that list only on the service's `closed` answer or on the loss of the connection (`close_answer` and `forget_closing` in `packages/host/tauriv2/src/sidecars.rs`, `closeAnswered` and `forgetClosing` in `packages/host/wailsv3/src/sidecars.go`), so core keeps the order that [sidecar messages](spec/sidecars.md#messages) require and the two hosts relay the answer the same way. In the service (sidecars/vt 80b45b2), `PersistentRegistry::close_surface` in `vt-core/src/protocol.rs` sends `SurfaceCommand::SessionClose` into the surface actor's queue, starts a task that awaits the actor, and returns `Ok`; the connection loop then writes `{surface, closed: true}` at once. The actor closes the PTY session (`PtyService::close` in `vt-core/src/pty.rs`, which waits for the reaper thread's `wait`) only when it takes that command from its queue, so the answer can precede the reap; the order depends on the actor's work at that moment, which makes the failure intermittent and independent of the host. The run's logs agree: neither host log has a `sidecar … close <surface>: …` line, and both host logs have the same four `connection lost; restarted` lines, so the Tauri closes were answered without error and not cleared by a connection loss. The service log has no timestamps or close lines. Two further service orders have the same form: the connection without a registry sends `SessionClose` without awaiting the actor (`close_connection_surface`), and `PtyService::close` that takes the child lock before a new session's reaper thread does returns after `kill` without reaping. The correction belongs to the service repository; core is unchanged. The correction belongs to the terminal service repository as its item S20; F61 stays open until S20 is released and `closing terminal tabs reaps every PTY child without killing the shared service` passes on both hosts with that service. Accepted in the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05 (core a3498ed4, terminal service b9b46c4, terminal plugin dfd2858, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 26 to 47; 339 of 344 checks passed) with S20, S21 and S22 of the terminal service: `closing terminal tabs reaps every PTY child without killing the shared service` passed on both hosts.
- [o] F62 — P1: Find why the Wails persistent transport harness waited for a connection event that never came. Found on 2026-10-05 while F59 was verified (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 45): `TestPersistentTransportHarnessEndpointAuthConcurrentReconnectAndCloseAck` failed at its 120s limit with `sidecars_transport_test.go:205: no connection event; the test stalled`, and passed in both configurations of `host-contract-check` of the same run, 3 of 3 alone and in the next full run. A stall is a missing event, not a slow one, so it is not load. Log: `~/backup/soksak-check-logs/f59-20261005/f59c-go.txt`. Resolved on 2026-10-05: the stall was a test race, not a missing host event. The service fixture `serveHarnessConnections` closed the first two connections that it accepted, after their first echo, and assumed that these were the first connections of the two hosts. When the first host's revived connection reached the service before the second host's first connection, the fixture closed the revived connection and kept the second host's connection open, so the second host lost no connection and published no connection event; the failed log has one `connection lost; restarted` line instead of two. The host publishes a connection event for each lost connection in this order. The fixture now selects the connection to close by its request: it closes a connection after it echoes an `open` request, and a revived connection, which carries `reconnect`, stays open; it also records its first error under a mutex. The Tauri harness already closes a connection only on the host's own `drop` request and has no such interleaving, so it is unchanged. The test gained the subtest `second opens after the first reconnected`, which opens the second host only after the first host's connection event. Red with the unchanged fixture: `sidecars_transport_test.go:190: no connection event; the test stalled` at 120.01s. Green after the correction: the same test 3 of 3 and the Wails host test package 1 of 1, on macOS 26.6.2 arm64.
- [o] F63 — P2: Find why the command supervisor's cleanup failed with `kill EPERM` after forwarding SIGTERM. Found on 2026-10-05 while F59 was verified: `forwards CLI SIGTERM to command cancellation and cleanup` (`scripts/test/test-command.test.mjs`) failed, and passed 3 of 3 alone and in the next full run. Log: `~/backup/soksak-check-logs/f59-20261005/f59c-pnpm.txt`. Resolved on 2026-10-05: the failing result was `fail` with the error `kill EPERM` and the only cleanup observation `verify` EPERM, so the refused call was the cleanup's existence probe `kill(-pgid, 0)`, not a signal; the line `SIGKILL to process group …: kill EPERM` of the same log belongs to the earlier test that injects that refusal. In XNU `killpg1` (`bsd/kern/kern_sig.c`) finds the group, skips members in state `SZOMB` and answers EPERM for a POSIX `kill` that found no member; a process leaves its group only when its parent reaps it (`reap_child_locked` in `kern_exit.c`). The command's descendant handles SIGTERM, so a SIGKILL of the supervisor ended it (the forced kill 100 ms after the forwarded SIGTERM or the cleanup's); its parent, the command, had already exited on SIGTERM, so launchd reaps it, and the group held only that zombie until launchd did, which took longer than the 300 ms of probes on the loaded machine; a group of this user's processes has no member with other credentials. On macOS 26.6.2 a group whose only member is an unreaped zombie answers EPERM for signal 0 and SIGKILL and ESRCH after the reap. The supervisor now reads the group's members from the process table after a refused probe (`groupMembers` in `scripts/test-command.mjs`), records them in the `verify` observation, and counts the group as cleaned when no listed member runs; a running member keeps the EPERM failure. The tests judge a descendant as ended by its process state, because `kill(pid, 0)` succeeds for a zombie. [Examples](operations/examples.md) states the rule. Red: `counts a process group that holds only zombies as gone after a denied probe` failed with `'fail' !== 'pass'` and the error `kill EPERM`; Green: it, `reads the members of a group from the real process table after a denied probe` and the 20 supervisor tests pass, and the four affected tests pass 3 of 3 in `make node-repeat`.
- [o] F64 — P1: Find why the files sidecar exited with SIGPIPE while Wails stopped it. Found in the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05 (a3498ed4): `the application log file holds the lines the page reports` failed on Wails with the host line `error: sidecar @soksak/sidecar-files: exited while stopping: signal: broken pipe`, which F47 made visible. Cause: when the host stopped its sidecars it removed their surfaces from the closing list, and a standard-input sidecar that answered such a close on its way out was taken as a protocol violation (`unexpected close answer`), so the host stopped reading and closed the pipe; the sidecar's next write got SIGPIPE, which the host wrote as `exited while stopping: signal: broken pipe`. In Tauri, `stop` also emptied the running list, so every message during the stop was an `unknown surface` violation, and a violation during the stop was dropped without a line. Fix (both hosts): the host keeps the surfaces and the removed closes of a stopping sidecar, accepts their answers and messages, reads the output to its end, writes a violation during the stop as `failed: <reason>` without a failure event, writes a nonzero or signalled end as `exited while stopping: exit status <code>` or `signal <number>` through the new platform operation `ExitStatus`/`exit_status`, and writes a forced kill as `did not end within the stop timeout and was killed`; [sidecars](spec/sidecars.md) states the stop. Red: Go `TestStopReadsOutputToItsEnd` logged `exited while stopping: signal: broken pipe` and the sidecar could not finish its writes, `TestStopReportsExitStatus` logged `signal: terminated`; Rust `stop_reads_output_to_its_end` (writes not finished) and `stop_reports_exit_status` (empty log) failed; Green: all pass and `make host-contract-check` passes 371 cases. Its acceptance is the next full window run without the line. Accepted in the thirteenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (eb707869, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 58 to 93; 334 of 344 checks passed): no `exited while stopping` line.
- [o] F65 — P1: Find why the card header control did not open a folded left sidebar on Wails. Found in the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05 (a3498ed4): `the card header has a fold control for each sidebar the card shows` failed after 20s with `the header control did not open the folded left sidebar again`; `core.grid` still reported the left sidebar `collapsed` and `requestedCollapsed`. Progress on 2026-10-05: the click did not run the command. The host log records no command, but the stored choice shows it: `core.card.sidebar.toggle` stores the opposite of the shown state, so a second toggle would have stored `collapsed: false`, and `requestedCollapsed: true` means no second toggle ran; no space fold applies, because `autoCollapsed` is false. Every draw of the card header moved both fold controls: `drawSideToggles` in `packages/workbench/plane.js` inserted each control before the card tools unless it already stood directly before them, which holds for at most one control, so with the top and left sides shown each draw moved the top and the left control with `insertBefore`. `insertBefore` takes a node out of the document before it inserts it again, and WebKit clears the target of a press when its node leaves the document (`EventHandler::nodeWillBeRemoved` sets `m_clickNode` to null), so the release sends no `click`. The check presses and releases through two host requests, and the draw of the first fold runs at an animation frame after its native preparation (F43) while `core.grid` already reports the stored fold, so that draw could fall between the second press and its release; Tauri passed because its draw did not fall there. The control now moves only when its order is wrong: from the last shown control backwards, a control moves only when its next sibling is not the next control (the card tools for the last), and the rule is stated in [exposure](spec/exposure.md#user-interface). No host change is needed, so the hosts have no Red test. Red: `a draw keeps the pressed card header fold control in the document` (`packages/workbench/test/plane-side-toggles.test.mjs`) failed with the removed controls `["top", "left"]` against the expected `[]` for the held draw of a left fold; Green: it passes, and the 301 workbench tests pass. Acceptance: a full window run in which the check passes on both hosts. Accepted on 2026-10-05 (8d9770e8 and 9a5e862d, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 15): `the card header has a fold control for each sidebar the card shows` passed 3 of 3 runs on both hosts.

- [o] F68 — P1: Write the WebKit child record without losing a write when page loads overlap. Found in the twelfth full window run of 2026-10-05 (5b0107ec) and its rerun of the failed files: Wails logged `error: webkit children record: rename: rename …/webkit-children.json.new …/webkit-children.json: no such file or directory` in `split, resize, reload, and WebView churn stay bounded`, in both runs. Cause: `RefreshWebKitChildren` runs from the navigation callback of each window, which Wails calls on its own goroutine, and every write used the same `.new` file, so the first rename took the file of the other writers and their renames failed. The race was older than F59; F47 made it an error line. Fix: both hosts write the record through one serialized function (`WriteWebKitRecord`, `write_record`), so Tauri, whose diagnostics build can defer the refresh, follows the same contract. Contract case `webkit-children.record.concurrent-refreshes`. Red: 15 of 32 concurrent Go writes and the concurrent Rust writes failed with `rename: … no such file or directory`; Green: both tests pass 3 of 3 and both host suites pass. Its acceptance is the next full window run without the rename line. Accepted in the thirteenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (eb707869, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 58 to 93; 334 of 344 checks passed): no `webkit children record` line.

The answer normally takes milliseconds, so 20s exceeds 100 times the expected time and is not classified as load; the work that held the main thread is to be recorded and found. Step 1 on 2026-10-05: a window check request that does not answer within its limit now records the host's threads at that moment with macOS `sample` into `<config-dir>/logs/stall-<pid>-<time>.txt` and names the file in its error (`e2e/stall-sample.mjs`, `within` in `e2e/app.mjs`), so the next occurrence shows what held the main thread. Red: `a request that does not answer within its limit records what the host was doing and names the record` and `a failed sample is named in the timeout instead of hiding it` failed against the earlier `within`; Green: the four tests of `e2e/test/stall-sample.test.mjs` and the 89 e2e unit tests pass, and a sample of the running Wails check host recorded its `com.apple.main-thread` stack. Another occurrence on 2026-10-05 at load average 132, while F25.1 was verified on Tauri: `diagnostics.fixture` and `status.get core.verify` failed with `main did not reply within 10000 ms`, and the late replies then logged `error: page: exposure reply does not match a pending request`; that was the page, which `sample` of the host does not show, so the WebContent process of the page is to be recorded too. Step 2 on 2026-10-05: a stall now also records the page's WebContent processes that the host's `webkit-children.json` lists, and a request that the host ends with `did not reply within` (a page that did not answer) records them too, naming the files or the reason they could not be made (`pageProcesses` and `sampleStall` in `packages/window-check/stall-sample.mjs`). The fourteenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (c2f21e69, apps eb707869) reproduced the Tauri page stall (`status.watch core.verify: main did not reply within 10000 ms`, then `exposure reply does not match a pending request`), but the record was lost: the host's WebKit record still listed WebContent process 52405, which had ended after an earlier reload, and its failed sample discarded the host's sample too. Each process is now sampled on its own and a process that cannot be sampled is named; Red: `a page process that already ended does not cost the records of the host and the other pages` failed; Green: it passes. Correction on 2026-10-05: the host's sample of that stall was not lost; the harness wrote `stall-36398-1791170946023.txt` before the page sample failed and only its error did not name the file. In that sample all 1,708 samples of the host's main thread wait in `mach_msg2_trap` under `-[NSApplication run]`, so the host's main thread was idle and did not cause the stall; the page that did not answer is the next record to read. Repeated on 2026-10-05 (core d26c53f8, apps restarted on that build, macOS 26.6.2 arm64): `application-log.test.mjs` `the application log file holds the lines the page reports` passed 5 of 5 on Tauri (`repeat`); the stall occurs only in full runs. Recurred in the sixteenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (16d699ec, load average up to 218 on 11 processors) on Wails, directly after `split-load-memory.test.mjs`: `the terminal applies the first installed family of font.family` failed with `status.watch core.verify: the document did not reply within 10s`, and the document's reply arrived later (`exposure reply 12799 has no matching request`). The records were written: all 1,017 samples of the host's main thread wait in `mach_msg2_trap` under `-[NSApplication run]` (`stall-3552-1791192586146.txt`), and the main thread of the page process 22225 waits in its run loop in 1,327 of 1,366 samples (`stall-3552-1791192586146-page-22225.txt`); the listed page 17819 had ended. Neither the host nor that page held its main thread, and the reply was late, not lost; the document's own process and its scheduling are to be read next. With F79 on 2026-10-06 (928c92b6 in development, load average 26 to 32), the first `e2e/balance.test.mjs` run on a Wails check app started a minute earlier logged `exposure reply 197 arrived 28670 ms after it was sent; its request timed out after 10000 ms`: the page answered a relayed request almost 29 s late, and the next three runs passed.
- [o] F70 — P2: Write each Wails binding failure once and in the error form. Found in the same logs: Wails writes `10:27AM ERR Binding call failed: Bound method returned an error: …` from its own logger for every binding call that returns an error, in addition to the page's line for the same failure, and Tauri writes no such line; F47 recorded that every Wails error goes through its error handler, which this path does not. Cause found on 2026-10-05 in the Wails v3.0.0-beta.27 source: `HTTPTransport.httpError` (`pkg/application/transport_http.go`) logs every error that it returns to the page with `t.logger.Error(err.Error())`, and the same `t.error` also logs the transport's own write failures, which no request receives, so the host cannot tell the two apart without matching message text. The correction belongs to the framework: `httpError` should not log at error level an error that it returns to its caller. That needs a change to Wails (a fork or an upstream change), which is the user's decision; core uses upstream Wails. Decided by the user on 2026-10-05: fork Wails in the account min-median-max and correct it there. Done on 2026-10-05: the branch `soksak/http-error-log` of `min-median-max/wails` (e8da589c, from v3.0.0-beta.27) removes the log line of `httpError`, so an error returned to the caller is not logged and a failed write of the error response still is; `apps/wailsv3/go.mod` and `packages/host/wailsv3/go.mod` replace `github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3` with that commit. Red: `TestHTTPTransportErrorIsReturnedNotLogged` of the fork failed against v3.0.0-beta.27 with `the returned error was also logged: "... Invalid runtime call: missing object value"`; Green: it and the `pkg/application` tests pass, and core's consumer test `TestTheTransportReturnsAFailedCallWithoutLoggingIt` failed against v3.0.0-beta.27 with `the transport logged the failure it returned` and passes with the fork. Observed on 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64): `core.plugins.install` of a plugin missing from the registry wrote `ERR Binding call failed: Bound method returned an error: plugin no-such-plugin is not in the registry` in the log of the 0.0.3 Wails release and no such line in the log of the debug build with the fork.

- [o] F92 — P1: Find why the drag lag of `outside.test.mjs` `native content, cards, and the sidebar rail stay aligned` exceeds its p90 limit on a 60 Hz display. Found on 2026-10-07 (core ade5cc5b, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, main display 2560×1440 at 60 Hz and scale 1): the three full window runs of that day and two runs of the check alone failed on both hosts with p90 55.9 to 58.0 ms against the limit of 3 frames (50.0 ms), while the median stayed at 41.0 to 42.6 ms within 2.5 frames; load average 7 to 18 on 11 processors. Each transaction is presented about 30 ms (2 frames) after it begins. The frame limits of [native surfaces](spec/native-surfaces.md) were set on 2026-10-01 (09127522) before the display changed, and the failure occurs at moderate load in every run, so it is not classified as load until the frames of the late steps are measured. Measured in the same runs: consecutive layout transactions begin about 33 ms (2 frames at 60 Hz) apart, for example #4300 to #4303 at −7.5, +24.4, +57.6 and +91.2 ms, because the page begins the next preparation only after the previous transaction was presented, while `diagnostics.drag` sends a step every 16 ms; the screen therefore shows a new layout every second frame and the frame between them shows the earlier layout one frame longer, which puts the 90th percentile above 3 frames. The [native surfaces](spec/native-surfaces.md) contract states the limits at 60 Hz, so the cadence of the transactions has to fit one frame, or the steps that the screen cannot show have to be measured against the presented layouts; which one is decided by the measurement of a transaction's stages at 60 Hz. The classification of this check as load in the record of F46 is replaced by this item. Measured on 2026-10-07 with `transactionCadence` (`e2e/drag-measurement.mjs`), which `outside.test.mjs` now prints before it judges the lag: over one drag the transactions began at a median interval of 33.4 ms (Wails, 47 transactions) and 33.3 ms (Tauri, 46), and each took a median 30.6 ms and 30.1 ms from its beginning to its presentation (load average 12). In the page's layout trace the next preparation begins about 1.5 ms after a presentation, so the interval is spent waiting for the animation frame after the preparation and for the presentation of that frame. Because a newer preparation extends the window's open transaction ([native surfaces](spec/native-surfaces.md#placement-sequence)), beginning it before the earlier commit would join both layouts in one commit, so the wait between the presentation and the next animation frame is the part to measure next. The layout trace now records `requested`, the time the page asks the host to wait for the presentation of its drawn DOM (`surfaceLayoutAfterPresentation`; [endpoint](spec/endpoint.md), contract case `diagnostics.capture-stop.payload-preserves-layout-stages`, Red in the Go and Rust cases with the five-stage record, Green after the change; `surface_layout_test` and `window_titlebar_reload_test` read the record with `SURFACE_LAYOUT_TRACE_STAGES`, which also removes their writes past four values). Measured on both hosts at load average 15: from the beginning to the request a median 17.8 ms (p90 18.8), from the request to the presentation 12.7 ms (13.5). The presentation is confirmed at the refresh that shows the drawn frame, so no refresh is lost there; the next preparation begins about 1.5 ms after that confirmation, after the animation frame of that refresh has run, and its draw waits for the following one. A cadence of one frame needs the earlier transaction to commit when WebKit hands the drawn frame's layers to the UI process rather than after the refresh shows it; the WebKit presentation callbacks are to be read next. Read in the WebKit source (main, 2026-10-07): `-[WKWebView _doAfterNextPresentationUpdate:]` calls `WebPageProxy::callAfterNextPresentationUpdate`, which sends `DrawingArea::DispatchAfterEnsuringDrawing` to the WebContent process; `RemoteLayerTreeDrawingArea` adds the reply to the commit bundle of its next rendering update, and `RemoteLayerTreeDrawingAreaProxy::commitLayerTree` runs the reply right after it applies that layer tree, inside the same Core Animation transaction, not when the screen shows the frame. The host registers the wait only when the page reports its draw, after the rendering update that contains the draw has committed, so the reply rides the next rendering update; that is the 12.7 ms from the request to the presentation, and the native commit comes one update after the DOM. Registering the wait before the draw attaches it to the update that runs the draw only if no rendering update runs between the registration and the page's animation frame; a rendering update in between would commit the native layout one frame before its DOM, which the [placement sequence](spec/native-surfaces.md#placement-sequence) forbids, so the correction has to bind the reply to the update that contains the draw. Measured with `native/darwin/tests/presentation_order_test.m` (60 Hz, load average 4): a page posts a script message in the animation frame that draws, and the UI process registers the presentation wait as soon as the message arrives; the confirmation came before the next refresh, that is with the commit of the drawn update, in 26, 24 and 21 of 40 draws in three runs, so the arrival of a script message and the commit of the update that sent it have no fixed order. `RemoteLayerTreeDrawingArea::dispatchAfterEnsuringDrawing` starts a rendering update on a zero-delay timer when the wait arrives, so a wait registered with the preparation, before the page draws, can attach to an update without the draw. With these WebKit interfaces the host cannot bind its commit to the update that contains the draw; the current order (register after the draw, commit with the next update while the open transaction holds the DOM) is the one that keeps the DOM and the native layout together, and at 60 Hz it gives a transaction every second frame. Meeting the 60 Hz limits of the contract therefore needs a decision: change the contract to that cadence, or a different presentation design that WebKit does not offer through these interfaces. Correction and completion on 2026-10-07: the conclusion above that these WebKit interfaces cannot give a transaction every frame at 60 Hz was wrong. The record of G1.4-14-4-2 measured this check at 60 Hz on 2026-10-01 with a median of 20–35 ms and a 90th percentile of 27–45 ms, with native commits 5–8 ms after each step, and that record was not read before the conclusion. The cause is F43 (ac8fb675, 2026-10-05): `drawPrepared` drew in the next animation frame, which waits for the display refresh, while a draw made outside a rendering update is carried by the rendering update that the host's presentation wait starts at once (`dispatchAfterEnsuringDrawing`); F43 stated that its change added no frame, which missed that update. The page now draws a prepared layout in the next task (`nextTask` in `packages/workbench/layout-queue.js`), which never runs inside a rendering update and its observation round, so the protection of F43 holds ([native surfaces](spec/native-surfaces.md#placement-sequence)); `animationFrame` and its 10-second error are removed ([native host](spec/native-host.md)). Red: `outside.test.mjs` failed on both hosts with a 90th percentile of 56–58 ms and a transaction interval of 33.4 ms, and `a prepared draw runs in the next task, not in the checkpoint that answered its preparation` (`packages/workbench/test/layout-queue.test.mjs`) failed without `nextTask`. Green: the 310 workbench tests pass; after both hosts were rebuilt the check passes 3 of 3 on each host with transactions 16.7 ms apart and 90th percentiles of 36.7–37.5 ms (Wails) and 20.1–20.8 ms (Tauri) at load average 7 to 9 on the 60 Hz display, and `outside.test.mjs`, `files.test.mjs`, `projects.test.mjs` and the padding check of `terminal.test.mjs` pass without a ResizeObserver loop error. `presentation_order_test` remains as the measurement that a script message and its commit have no fixed order.

    - [o] V5-51-1 — P0: Inject shell integration and clear the prompt region on resize from OSC 133 marks. Acceptance: the sidecar starts zsh and bash with integration that emits OSC 133 prompt and command marks without changing the user's configuration files; on a resize while the cursor is in a marked prompt, the engine clears the marked prompt rows before reflow and the shell redraws; a window check resizes a wrapped zsh and bash input line on both hosts and finds no residue (V5-48); shells without integration keep the current behavior, which the specification states. Done on 2026-09-25. The alacritty engine applies each OSC 133 mark at its position in the byte stream, moves the cursor to a new line on `A` when it is not at column 0, keeps a prompt or output state, and rejects `redraw` values other than `0`, `1`, and `last`. On a primary-screen resize in the prompt state it reflows, clears the rows from the first row of the cursor's logical line to the bottom, and places the cursor as many rows below that row as it was before the reflow. It clears after the reflow, not before as this item first stated, because the reflowed logical line and cursor exist only after the reflow. The cursor placement is measured: zsh and readline both move up by the cursor row count of the width they last drew at; with the cursor left in place zsh drew one row low, and with the cursor at the first row bash overwrote the output row above the prompt. The sidecar starts zsh with `ZDOTDIR` pointing at an embedded `.zshenv` and bash with an exported `PROMPT_COMMAND` entry that sources an embedded script. Measured bash 3.2 behavior shaped the script: `--posix` does not read `ENV` unless the shell runs as `sh`; a file read by `source` does not see the `DEBUG` trap and a trap it sets is replaced by an earlier one, so the entry records the trap before `source`; `$(builtin trap -p)` does not show the parent's traps; `LINENO` advances on each line of `PROMPT_COMMAND`, so the first attempt reported an empty input line as a command; an entry ending in a newline broke `PROMPT_COMMAND` extended as macOS recommends (`"$PROMPT_COMMAND; x"`); and a `SIGWINCH` during startup made the trap run for a command after the first `A`. Red: the engine tests `a_resize_in_the_prompt_state_clears_the_cursor_logical_line_to_the_bottom`, `redraw_last_places_the_cursor_as_redraw_1_does`, `redraw_last_scrolls_the_screen_when_the_offset_row_is_below_the_bottom`, `prompt_rows_that_the_reflow_moved_into_the_scrollback_are_cleared`, `a_prompt_start_moves_a_cursor_off_column_zero_to_the_next_line`, and `an_unsupported_redraw_value_is_rejected_without_a_state_change` failed first; `tests/shell_test.rs` failed on each bash defect above; `tests/shell_redraw_test.rs` (real zsh and bash with the engine) showed the overwritten row; and the window check failed on both hosts with `START-` shown three times while the first prompt had reported a command start. Green: engine tests 79 of 79, `shell_test.rs` 7 of 7, `shell_redraw_test.rs` 2 of 2, and the sidecar workspace tests pass; on rebuilt Wails and Tauri the window checks `a resize redraws a wrapped zsh input line without rows of the previous width` and the bash case pass with a narrowing, a widening, and a divider drag (three runs per host), `e2e/terminal.test.mjs` and `e2e/terminal-font.test.mjs` pass 62 of 62, and `pnpm test`, `make native-test`, and the structural checks pass. A second size change before the shell redraws can still make the shell draw at a width that is no longer current (measured with bash 3.2 at 30, 45, and 60 columns in the sidecar test); the real-input tier was not run for this change.

      - [o] V5-51-6-1 — P1: Keep the page's cursor state equal to the drawn cursor. On 2026-09-25 the protocol check found on Tauri that after `terminal.focus` the region was the native first responder while `terminal.cursor.focused` stayed false until the next output, and `terminal.cursor.shape` reported the configured policy instead of the shape a program requested with DECSCUSR. Acceptance: the measured cause, a fix, contract and plugin tests, and the window check on both hosts. Done on 2026-09-25. Cause: `present_screen` sent only the raster; the callers that changed the screen through output, scrolling, or input also sent the screen event, but focus, theme, cursor-policy, selection, and configuration redraws did not, so the page kept the previous cursor. A `screen.read` request showed the sidecar already focused. The page also copied only the position, visibility, and focus from the screen cursor. Fix: `present_screen` sends the screen event of every raster it presents, the callers send a screen event themselves only when no image region exists, and `terminal.cursor` reports `drawn` (shape and blink request after the program's request and the focus rule). Red: the contract test `a_focus_change_sends_the_screen_with_the_presentation_that_draws_it` (an idle sidecar answered the focus change without a screen event) and the plugin test `the drawn cursor follows the screen event while the policy shape stays` failed before the change.
