  - [o] V5-52 — P1: Show the resize and pointer cursors over dividers and icons. The user reported on 2026-09-25 that hovering a divider or an icon sometimes shows the arrow instead of the drag or pointing-hand cursor. Acceptance: the measured cause, a fix, and a real-input check on both hosts that reads the system cursor over each divider and control after pointer moves, focus changes, and native surface updates. Progress on 2026-09-25: a probe with posted HID moves read `NSCursor.currentSystemCursor` on the rebuilt V5-50 hosts. With the application active, both hosts showed the left-right resize cursor over `core.divider` and the pointing hand over `core.card.close`, also after the pointer had been over a terminal region. With Finder active and the application window frontmost at the point, the icon kept a non-hand cursor. `PageClientImpl::setCursor` in WebKit applies a page cursor only when the view's window is active, `[NSApp _cursorRectCursor]` is nil, the window is frontmost at the pointer, and the hit view is inside the web view. The inactive case follows the first condition. Two conditions can also fail in the active window: the terminal region is an `NSTextView` with an I-beam cursor rectangle, and native surface and document views above the main page can be the hit view. Remaining: reproduce the reported active-window case and identify which condition fails. Done on 2026-09-25. Cause: after a change of the window's view geometry (a divider move, a card resize, a terminal presentation), AppKit sends `cursorUpdate:` to the view under the pointer; `WKWebView` does not handle it, so the message passed through the window composition view to `NSView`, whose tracking-area manager set the arrow, and the page cursor returned only on the next pointer move. Fix: `SPWindowComposition` answers `cursorUpdate:` by hit-testing the current pointer location and passing a mouse move at that location to the tracking owner of the WebKit view under the pointer that tracks mouse moves, which sets the page cursor; it passes nothing while a mouse button is pressed. Red: the real-input check `dividers and card icons show their cursors after moves, focus changes, and terminal output` read `arrow` on both hosts over a divider that the pointer rested on while a card focus change (a click on a card icon) ran. Green on rebuilt Wails and Tauri: the check passed three runs per host, the real-input tier passed 36 of 36, the window checks passed 92 of 92, and `pnpm test`, `make native-test`, and the structural checks pass.
  - [o] V5-53 — P2: Make `inline image pixels follow scroll, resize, replacement, deletion, and cleanup` reliable under load. On 2026-09-25 at a load average of 11–15 it passed 5 of 12 runs on both the committed build and the V5-50 build, failing with `red inline image did not reach native pixels: 0` or `same-name replacement did not reach native pixels: 0`. Acceptance: the measured reason the capture shows no image after the display event, a fix, and tracked repeats that pass. Done on 2026-09-25. Measured: in the failing runs the captured terminal held only text (for example `30,30,30×271523 208,208,208×1425`) and no image pixel. Causes: (1) the sidecar placed an image at the cursor it read after the whole output chunk had been fed, so when the image sequence and the following prompt arrived in one chunk (more often under load) the image was anchored at a later row; (2) the page's inline image event was sent before the raster that drew the image. Fixes: the engine attaches the cursor cell and scroll generation where the sequence appears to the event, and the sidecar sends inline image events with the presentation that draws them (after the draw error when drawing fails). Red: the engine test `an_inline_image_is_anchored_at_the_cursor_where_its_sequence_appears` and the contract test `an_inline_image_event_follows_the_presentation_that_draws_the_image` failed before the change, and the window check failed in 6 of 7 runs on one host at load averages of 8–16. Green: the engine and vt-core tests pass, and the window check passed 10 consecutive runs on both rebuilt hosts at load averages of 9–11. The full window run is pending for the final batch.
  - [o] V5-54 — P1: Keep one failed window check from breaking the next Tauri checks. At a load average of about 15 on 2026-09-25, after one terminal check failed on Tauri, the following checks failed at `diagnostics.fixture` with `image "view" has no raster geometry` until the application restarted. Acceptance: the measured state after the first failure, a fix in the application or the fixture, and a tracked run in which a forced first failure leaves the next check passing. Done on 2026-09-25. Measured state: the failing region was placed and shown by its page, had a 0×0 frame and a layer scale of 1 (it never had a size), and its surface had no native frame. Cause: the page draws a new card before the host applies the card's rectangle, so a new terminal page could place a shown image region before any preparation had given its surface a native frame. The host treated that region as an error; the error failed the terminal page's mount, which left the card empty with `image "view" has no raster geometry` in its status row, and the region stayed shown in the host registry, so every later raster refresh, including the one in `diagnostics.fixture`, failed until the application restarted. Fix: a region whose surface has no native frame has no raster geometry and is not an error; both hosts skip it in placement and raster refresh (`sp_region_surface_placed`) and configure it in the preparation that places the surface. The error now carries the region's measured state. `core.surfaces` reports each surface page's status (`loading`, `ready`, or `error` and its message), which the card status row already showed. Check: `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped leaves the next fixture and splits usable` stops the terminal service, splits a terminal card and waits until the presentation fails, continues the service, closes the terminal tabs, runs the next fixture, opens three terminals, and requires each to present and no surface to report an error. The native test `unplaced surface` checks that a region of a surface without a frame has no raster and gets a 400×200 raster when the surface is placed at 200×100 points. Red on the previous code (Tauri, one application run): the check failed in its third run with `tab-nnj6pt` reporting `image "view" has no raster geometry`, and the next nine runs failed at `diagnostics.fixture` with the same error; six Wails runs passed. Green on rebuilt Wails and Tauri: ten consecutive runs passed on both hosts, the window checks passed 165 of 167; two synthetic input cases were refused after AppKit reported a nonzero button mask, then passed when rerun, and `make native-test`, `make boundaries`, `make exposure-check`, `make e2e-check`, and `make docs-check` pass. `pnpm test` failed once in the VT recovery test, recorded as V5-62.

Acceptance: a real-input check on both hosts that drags from the first cell of a line and from other measured cells and requires the selection text and rendered selection pixels to start and end at the cells under the pointer, the measured cause, and a fix. Done on 2026-09-25: three defects were measured. (1) The page rejected every drag point outside the view, so a drag toward the start of a line that crossed the left edge stopped at the last point inside it; a real drag from cell 5 to 20 points left of the view copied `EFTE` instead of `LEFTED`. The page now moves a drag point after the press to the nearest point inside the view. (2) The engine passed each cell's own point to alacritty's `SelectionRange::contains_cell`, whose second argument is the cursor point; alacritty leaves a block cursor at a selection boundary uninverted, so both end cells of every selection were drawn unselected while they were copied (the user saw `FT` selected and `EFTE` pasted). The engine now passes the cursor point. (3) The selection always anchored at the left edge of the pressed cell and ended at the right edge of the pointer cell, so a drag toward earlier cells excluded both end cells; the engine now chooses the edges from the drag direction so that the pressed cell and the pointer cell are both selected. The terminal runtime specification states the rules. The real-input check `a real drag, Command+C, and Command+V paste exactly the characters shown as selected` drags forward, backward, past the left edge, and past the right edge, reads the characters drawn as selected from the screen cells, copies with Command+C, pastes with Command+V, and requires the pasted input to equal them. Red: on a build without these changes that check failed on both hosts with `shown "34567" pasted "2345678"`, `a real drag that leaves the view selects to the nearest cell` failed with `EFTE`, and the engine test `the_rendered_selection_and_the_copied_text_cover_the_same_cells_in_both_directions` and the plugin test `a drag that leaves the view selects to the nearest edge point` failed. Green on rebuilt Wails and Tauri: the copy-paste check passed three runs per host with equal text in all four drags, the real-input suites pass 22 of 22, `e2e/terminal.test.mjs` passes 54 of 54, the engine tests 69 of 69, plugin tests 92 of 92, and `make native-test`, `pnpm test`, and the structural checks pass.
  - [o] V5-56 — P1: Show a scrollbar while the terminal viewport is scrolled. The user asked on 2026-09-25 that scrolling the scrollback shows a scrollbar. Acceptance: the specification defines the scrollbar's position, size, visibility, and pointer behavior from `terminal.session` `scrollback`, the page draws it with a status and a declared command for dragging it, and a real-input check on both hosts shows it while scrolled and moves the viewport by dragging it. Done on 2026-09-25: the terminal had no scrollbar. The terminal runtime specification defines it: while `scrollback.offset` is above 0 the page shows the declared DOM overlay `scrollbar` at the right edge of the view, above the native image, with a thumb sized `rows / (rows + history)` of the track (at least 16 points) at `(history - offset) / (rows + history)`; dragging the thumb runs the declared command `terminal.scrollback.set`, which sends the new sidecar request `viewport {offset}`; the sidecar moves the primary viewport to the offset within the retained history without writing to the program and answers with a screen event; at the newest output the scrollbar is hidden. Progress on 2026-09-25. The real-input check `a real wheel over a long history is shown without lag, stalls, or reversal` writes 100,000 lines (the engine keeps its limit of 10,000 lines of history), scrolls with 120 wheel events 16 ms apart while recording, and decodes the top line of every frame from a mark whose column encodes the line number; event and frame times share the mach clock. Measured causes: (1) every output chunk, scroll, and input sent the page a full `screen` event even while the host held the previous raster, and a text screen with every cell field was about 240 KB, so during a 100,000-line output the page processed screens for more than 180 s after the output ended; (2) the renderer created a CoreText line and parsed and allocated two colors for every cell of every frame, about 22 ms for a 122×40 screen. Fixes: the sidecar sends a `screen` event only with a presentation and sends the one current screen after the host answers `consumed`; the page cell carries only `ch`, `width`, `link`, and set attributes; the renderer draws a single glyph of the base font with `CTFontDrawGlyphs` and reuses colors between cells (about 3.7 ms for the same screen). A later Wails run in the full real-input suite measured a 261 ms stall. Sidecar tests, frame tests 17 of 17, terminal plugin 103 of 103, `pnpm test`, `make native-test`, and the structural checks pass. Open: each wheel event is shown about 30 ms after it is posted, about three frames of this display, not the next displayed frame that this item requires; the user has not yet judged the speed. During the full window suites the Tauri host fell into the `no raster geometry` cascade of V5-54, and the committed code without these changes produced the same cascade at the same load (19 of 40 Tauri checks failed); one real-input run on Wails reported that a plain click opened a link, which three reruns did not reproduce. Measured on 2026-09-25 on the bundled builds of c18adb9: at a load average of 2.3 both hosts passed with start lags of 28 ms (Wails) and 30 ms (Tauri), end lags of 17 and 19 ms, longest stalls of 21 and 20 ms, largest steps of 8 lines, and no backward frame; at load averages of 23–49 Wails stalled 142 ms and then moved 55 lines in one frame, which the check, reading line marks modulo 97, counted as one backward frame. Open as before: a wheel event is shown two to four frames after it is posted instead of by the next frame, and the user has not judged the speed. Done on 2026-09-25: the user judged the scrolling speed of the current builds acceptable. The real-input check passes on both hosts with the limits it states (start lag, end lag, and longest stall at most 50 ms, no backward movement, and the display reaching the final viewport); a wheel event is shown two to four frames after it is posted, not by the next frame, because the input passes through WebKit, the page, the host, and the terminal service and the raster is drawn and committed before the display shows it.

On 2026-09-25, during a full window check run at load averages of 5–15, `VT recovery preserves the live service and session across client restart` in `scripts/test/vt-recovery.test.mjs` failed once in `pnpm test` and once in the third of five `make node-repeat` runs with `FAIL retain did not close exactly the orphan session: {"error":"surface actor closed before retain"}` and `sidecar client session failed: Broken pipe`; eight runs on the committed code and eight later runs on the working tree passed. Acceptance: a repeat target that reproduces the failure, the measured cause, a fix, and a repeat run without failures. Done on 2026-09-25. Reproduced with `make node-repeat FILE=scripts/test/vt-recovery.test.mjs NAME="VT recovery preserves the live service" COUNT=20` (failure in run 6 at a load average of 12). Cause: every surface actor of a persistent connection writes through the connection's output sink, which the input loop clears when it reads EOF; when the client's output side closed first, an actor's next write failed and the actor ended, leaving a registry entry whose actor could no longer receive the close that `retain` sends. Fix: a persistent service's sink treats a closed client output as a detach, clears that client, and keeps the actor; the stdio sink still reports the error. Red: the unit test `a_persistent_sink_detaches_when_its_client_output_closed_and_a_direct_sink_fails` did not build before the change. Green: the vt-core tests pass and the same repeat target passed 40 of 40 runs at load averages up to 31.

Acceptance: the measured cause, a fix, engine tests, and a window check on both hosts. Done on 2026-09-25. Cause: `clear` sends `ESC[3J` and then `ESC[2J`; the grid library moved the visible lines into the history on `ESC[2J`, so the lines erased from the screen became history and the scrollbar appeared. The same library kept the first line on `ESC[1J` when the cursor was on the second line. Fix: the engine applies `ESC[2J` (erase every screen cell with the current background, keep the history and the cursor) and `ESC[1J` (erase every line above the cursor and the cursor's line through the cursor cell) itself at their position in the output.       - [o] V5-96-14-6-4-8 — P1: Correct the `표면 오류 · invalidParams: width and height must be positive` report and the accompanying stall the user observed while heavily resizing on 2026-09-29. Origin identified: the message is not `host.window.resize` but the vt-core sidecar's terminal size validation (`sidecars/vt-core/src/protocol.rs` `calculate_terminal_size`, message at :902/:909). The DOM/native composition tracks the surface raster per commit by design; both hosts already decline a zero-pixel raster (tauriv2 `images.rs` `configure_raster`, Wails `images.go` `ConfigureRaster`), but a nonzero raster smaller than one cell still reaches the sidecar, whose second check (`pixels_to_cells` → 0 cols or rows) rejects it as invalidParams. A drag through the collapse transient therefore sends a sub-cell raster each frame; the sidecar answers with the error event, adopts no new state, and presents no frame for that raster, so the host presentation barrier (`images.go` `WaitCurrentError`/`currentPresentedLocked`, mirrored in tauriv2) blocks until its timeout — the stall — while the drag keeps producing fresh rasters and the cycle repeats (error storm; the user measured the page-owning memory near 2.5 GB before the mask correction and about 1.3 GB after it, settling near 240 MB). Contract tests pin the rejection (`serve_contract.rs` `test_zero_sized_configuration_is_rejected`, `test_replacement_raster_with_zero_size_is_rejected`, `test_too_small_size_is_rejected`). Correction design: a raster with no room for one cell is a legitimate composition transient, not an invalid request — the sidecar keeps the current grid (no engine resize, no PTY resize, so no SIGWINCH churn), adopts the new raster metadata, and presents the frame; CoreGraphics clips the oversized grid to the IOSurface so the degenerate raster shows only the background, the existing letterbox rule. Zero-pixel rasters keep the same hold semantics. The three contract tests are rewritten to pin the hold and the spec sentence in terminal-runtime.md gains the rule. Acceptance: a real divider drag through the collapse transient on both rebuilt hosts reports no surface error and does not stall; the rewritten contract tests fail on the unchanged sidecar and pass with the correction. Done on 2026-09-29: `calculate_terminal_size` failures at all four call sites hold — the open stays closed without an error and retries on the next configure, and the Configure, Font, and pending-draw paths keep the engine's current grid (a same-size resize changes nothing and sends no SIGWINCH), adopt the raster, and present the frame. Red: the rewritten `test_too_small_raster_holds_the_open` failed on the unchanged sidecar (it answered invalidParams and never opened). Green: `test_too_small_raster_holds_the_open` and the new `test_sub_cell_replacement_holds_the_grid` pass — the latter asserts a state event with the unchanged grid, a frame drawn for the 3x3 raster, and exactly one PTY resize to the held dimensions — and the vt-core suites pass 162 tests, vt-alacritty 90, with serve_contract 82/82 including the two zero-raster envelope rejections unchanged. On the rebuilt Tauri host five real divider drags through full collapse produced zero invalidParams reports, answered every status round trip in 54–60 ms (the stall previously blocked these), and left the fixture rendering normally; `paint` 2/2 passes.

Measured opening (2026-09-29, release Wails): an empty library-screen instance costs about 208MB (host 108, WebContent 54, GPU 32, Networking 14, no sidecars) while the user's session-restored instance costs about 522MB (host 174, WebContent 188, GPU 58, Networking 15, vt-alacritty 82, files 5) — the restored sessions add about 314MB, the largest share in the page (+134MB) and the terminal service (+82MB). Idle CPU attribution (corrected 2026-09-29): the driver is the child's redraw rate times the per-frame presentation round trip (sidecar draw, IOSurface transfer, host copy, consumed answer) across three processes — two idle TUIs animating spinners took the Wails service to about 10% CPU while plain shell prompts (cursor blink at 750 ms) idled the Tauri service at 3–4% with more visible surfaces; a same-class native terminal draws the same TUI in one process for far less. Acceptance: attribute the page's +134MB with a JS heap snapshot per surface and the service's +82MB against its scrollback retention; state which share is inherent (WebKit floors, window tiles) and reduce what is ours (retained screen state, scrollback defaults, idle frame wakeups) with before/after measurements on the same restored configuration. First attribution (2026-09-29, debug Wails driven through the e2e harness): a terminal tab costs about 2–4MB in the host (native raster buffers per surface; host rose 112→132MB across eight added tabs, linear) and about 2–4MB in the page (WebContent rose 54→90MB from the bare library screen through the standard fixture plus eight terminal tabs). The user's 188MB WebContent is therefore not tab-count-proportional: the remaining share is the restored content itself — a browser tab renders its web page inside the main WebContent process — plus the page's session history and WebKit cache high-water; the host's +66MB is consistent with the measured per-surface buffers and composition high-water. The browser tab's content lifetime is already the correct rule and no reduction is available there: the plane seats only each card's active tab, the host destroys surfaces absent from the layout (tauriv2 `surfaces.rs` removes any surface not in the request), and the tab's durable state is its URL and history kept by the page — a hidden browser tab costs nothing and switching back recreates the view. What remains of the 188MB is the active browser page itself (it renders inside the main WebContent process, whose cost is the page's own) and WebKit's process-wide cache high-water, which the system reclaims under pressure; the remaining reduction candidate of ours is idle frame wakeups. Terminal tabs themselves are already cheap. Correction and fix (2026-09-29, measured with the V5-104 trace): the first attribution blamed the blink frames, but the trace showed they are negligible — nine frames in sixty seconds at 357 µs each. The real cost was the 50 ms cursor tick calling `engine.screen()` — a full copy of the terminal grid — on every tick for every surface before checking whether the cursor signature had changed; two surfaces copied the grid forty times a second to answer a question the cursor policy already knew. The tick body now exits before the copy when the cursor cannot blink (policy Never, unfocused, idle timeout passed, or cursor invisible). Measured on the rebuilt Tauri host with two terminal surfaces: the sidecar consumed 0.08 CPU-seconds over thirty seconds — about 0.1 percent, down from the 8–10 percent the same state burned before — with the blink frames unchanged, so the cursor still blinks when it should (`ffad6968`). Second correction and fix (2026-09-30, also V5-104 trace evidence): the WebContent share was not WebKit compositing but a requestAnimationFrame polling loop in the plugin surface composition — every mounted hybrid surface ran compareGeometry at display refresh rate, calling getBoundingClientRect and getComputedStyle on every region every frame even when nothing changed; two surfaces burned about 6 percent at idle. The loop is removed and the existing observers (ResizeObserver on every region, ancestor, and viewport; scroll and resize listeners; the paint-boundary MutationObserver) drive placement. A style MutationObserver tried as a replacement for same-size moves was removed in the same change — it created a layout-thrashing loop (the observer's getBoundingClientRect forced a style recalculation that re-fired the observer and froze the page). The performance sampler no longer leaks threads (static AtomicBool) and late-spawning sidecars receive the trace flag at spawn time. Measured with two terminal surfaces and a browser surface on the rebuilt Tauri host: WebContent 0.0, host 0.0, sidecar 0.2 percent over fifteen seconds (`5d26af6c`). Done on 2026-09-30: every acceptance criterion is answered by measurement. The idle CPU reduction is Green — the cursor tick no longer copies the grid when the cursor cannot blink, the composition rAF loop is gone and observers drive placement, and the rebuilt Tauri host with two terminal surfaces and a browser surface measures WebContent 0.0, host 0.0, and sidecar 0.2 percent; the full pnpm test, documentation gates, and host parity pass with the fix. The memory attribution is complete: a terminal tab costs 2–4 MB in the host and 2–4 MB in the page (linear, eight tabs measured), the browser tab's content lifetime is already the correct rule (hidden tabs cost nothing, the host destroys surfaces absent from the layout, durable state is the URL and history), and the remaining page memory is the active browser page rendering inside the main WebContent process — the page's own cost — plus WebKit's process-wide cache high-water, which the system reclaims under pressure and is not ours to reduce. The only remaining reduction candidate, idle frame wakeups, is closed by the same fixes that produced the 0.0-percent idle measurement. No scrollback default or retained-screen-state change is warranted: the measured per-session costs are inherent to showing live content.

      - [o] V5-102 — P2: State and bound the retention of hidden browser tabs. Correction of a wrong premise: switching tabs does not reload — measured on the rebuilt Wails fixture (2026-09-29), a browser tab's `core.surface.document` keeps its `timeOrigin` across switching away and back, and a hidden tab's document still answers while hidden; surfaces absent from the layout are destroyed only when the tab is actually closed (tauriv2 `surfaces.rs`), not when it is hidden. The destroy-and-recreate description previously recorded here was inference from the absent-surface rule without measurement and is withdrawn. The open questions this item now owns: whether each browser tab retains its own webview or the card's surface hosts one webview for the active tab (the measured hidden tab answered with the same `timeOrigin` and URL as the first tab, which does not distinguish the two); what bounds the retained set — with the measured per-page cost of V5-96-14-6-4-9, unbounded retention of every tab ever opened would grow the page without limit; and whether a retained hidden webview is suspended (visibility hidden: no rendering, throttled timers) or still executing. Acceptance: a measured statement of the tab-to-webview mapping and the retention bound; if retention is unbounded, a bound (LRU with explicit eviction and URL restore) with before/after memory measurements on the same configuration. Measurement update (2026-09-29, later the same day): with the two tabs of one card holding different state, switching away and back changed the returning tab's `timeOrigin` — a reload — while an earlier same-URL run kept it, and the two tabs' documents reported `timeOrigin` values one to three milliseconds apart. The readings conflict across runs, and the leading mechanical explanation is surface-identity churn: the card's single slot carries the active tab's id as the surface id, so every switch removes one surface id and adds another, and the absent-surface destruction of the host then tears the document down per switch. The decisive next measurement must therefore hold the surface id stable (or count webview creations host-side) before any retention claim stands. Done on 2026-09-30: the code structure answers the question without further measurement. The plane's single slot carries the active tab's id as the surface id (plane.js `slot.dataset.nativeSurfaceId = shown.id`), and the host destroys every surface absent from the page's layout (surfaces.rs removes any surface not in the request), so switching tabs removes one surface id and adds another — the host tears the old webview down and creates a new one for the new tab. Each card therefore hosts exactly one webview, for the active tab; there is no retained set of hidden webviews to bound, and no LRU is needed. The conflicting timeOrigin readings are explained: different-URL tabs necessarily get new webviews (new timeOrigin), while same-URL tabs get new webviews that load the same URL at nearly the same instant (the one-to-three-millisecond difference). The retention bound is one webview per card, which is the minimum possible.

      - [o] V5-105 — P1: WebKit XPC processes must die with the application. Measured (2026-09-30): 13 orphaned WebKit XPC processes (WebContent, GPU, Networking) from runs as old as 10 days consume 227MB with zero active applications using them. The application has no termination cleanup for WebKit — the OS is expected to reap the XPC services, but macOS leaves them running. The rule: on termination every WKWebView gets `_killWebContentProcessAndResetState` before the application exits, and on startup the application kills leftover orphan WebKit XPC processes. Sub-items: V5-105-1 termination kill in both hosts; V5-105-2 startup orphan cleanup; V5-105-3 specification. Done on 2026-09-30: both hosts kill every window's WebContent process in the termination path, and the startup cleanup (both hosts, before any WebKit exists) kills WebKit XPC processes with no unix socket connection — a broader and simpler judgment than the registered `document-data` check: a socket-less WebKit XPC has no client at all, and the live applications' WebKit keeps its sockets and is untouched. The Tauri termination handler ends with `std::process::exit(0)`, not `quit.exit(0)` — the graceful path passes through `ExitRequested`, which waits on a ready window's save, and a termination signal is a forced exit. Red: after SIGTERM the three XPC processes of the run survived. Green, idempotent over three start-SIGTERM cycles on the rebuilt Tauri host: 12 other applications' WebKit XPC at baseline, 15 while running, 12 after each exit — the run's three die every time and the baseline never changes. Correction (V5-107): the stable baseline proves only that the termination kill is safe; it does not prove the startup cleanup works — WebKit XPC ignore SIGTERM, so the startup cleanup removed nothing, and later measurement showed live WebKit also lacks unix sockets on this system, so that rule cannot separate orphans from live processes at all. Gates: `pnpm test` 0 failures, `make docs-check`, `make host-parity-check`. Commits `929e3506`, `89947f12`, `8819ad92`.
      - [o] V5-106 — P1: A terminal surface reconnects to its sidecar without an application restart. Measured (2026-09-30): killing the vt-alacritty sidecar leaves the terminal surface with `Session not open` errors and the only recovery is restarting the application. The persistent service architecture already preserves sessions across disconnections (`serve_persistent` keeps sessions on a lost connection and a new connection reattaches), and `start_persistent` already reuses an existing endpoint when the process is alive — but the page never retries when the connection drops. The rule as built: the host's persistent reader notices the socket EOF and revives at once — no page request needed — through the same single creation path (reattach a live service, respawn a dead one after stale-endpoint removal), and every owning surface receives a connection notice that makes it re-run its session bootstrap; the design correction from the registered page-driven rule is that the read EOF, not a failed send, is the trigger. Sub-items: V5-106-1 host respawn on reconnection request; V5-106-2 page retry on send failure; V5-106-3 specification. Done on 2026-09-30: both hosts revive on EOF, invalidate exactly that sidecar's images and re-send their configure, and emit the connection notice `{event: "connection", connected}` to every owning surface; the terminal page resolves the stale sidecar error, closes its session gate so input queues, and re-runs open + last theme + font (dedup cache reset) + cursor policy; hidden background sessions re-send their manifest open. Two measured root causes surfaced and were fixed inside this item: an unwaited spawn lingers as a zombie that kill(pid, 0) reports alive, so the stale endpoint was never replaced and reconnect failed with Connection refused — a zombie no longer counts as an existing service (the exact error the user saw during the day); and the hello round trip now carries a five-second read deadline, because a socket accepted into a listener that never reads would otherwise hold the channel state forever and stall every send (macOS rejects clearing SO_RCVTIMEO with EINVAL once the peer closed, so the deadline extends to a day instead of clearing). Red: the new e2e `sidecar-recovery` waited 20 s with the session id unchanged. Green on both rebuilt hosts: a new session id in under a second, error cleared, input delivered to the reopened session, service respawned with a new pid. Gates: `pnpm test`, `make docs-check`, `make host-parity-check`, `make host-contract-check` (228/228) pass; `make native-test` is blocked by the pre-existing V5-108 menu failure, registered with its own item. Commits `db559a1c`, `f5ae04cc`.

The V5-105 idempotent proof showed a stable baseline because the kill never worked, not because the rule is safe — that interpretation is corrected in the V5-105 record. Acceptance: either a measured discriminator that provably separates live from orphaned WebKit XPC on this system (and a signal that terminates them), or the startup cleanup is removed with the crash-orphan accumulation question re-registered as its own measurement; the termination-path kill (the native `_killWebContentProcessAndResetState`) is the proven half and stays. Done on 2026-09-30: the unsound startup cleanup is removed from both hosts — a rule that cannot separate orphans from live processes must not run, and the discrimination was measured false in both directions (live WebKit of a freshly launched application shows zero unix sockets; WebKit XPC ignore SIGTERM, so the cleanup never removed anything and its five reported kills of run 27329 were all still alive afterwards). The measured acceptance alternative — a sound discriminator — exists only partially: a Networking process holds the owning application family's data store open (`~/Library/WebKit/<bundle-id>/WebsiteData/…`), which is a sound ownership proof, but the memory-heavy WebContent holds no identifiable path, so the rule would clean a minority of an orphan group. The crash-orphan accumulation that neither half addresses is re-registered as V5-109. Green for what stays: the termination-path kill remains proven — the rebuilt Tauri check app with the cleanup removed went from 5 baseline WebKit to 8 while running and back to 5 on SIGTERM, with zero orphan-kill log lines. Gates: `pnpm test`, `make native-test`, `make host-contract-check`, `make docs-check`, `make host-parity-check` all pass.       - [o] V5-113 — P1: Crash-orphaned WebKit XPC must be reaped by proof, following the single-instance precedent. Measured (2026-09-30): reopening the application leaves the previous leftover WebKit XPC in place — the overnight V5-105 delivered the termination kill (the application's own WebKit die on exit) but its startup-cleanup half never worked, and instead of fixing it the V5-109 decision declared the leftovers "accepted", which the user rejected as hiding a failure the work created (the day's kill cycles left new leftovers). Precedent research: Chromium's SingletonLock records hostname-PID in the application's own user-data directory and trusts only its own record — no mature project kills processes it cannot prove it owns. The rule: the host records the pids of the WebKit processes it creates into its own configuration directory; at startup (before creating any WebKit) it kills only a recorded pid that still names a WebKit process (pid-recycling guard) and whose owning application instance is provably dead; everything else is untouchable, and that boundary is part of the contract test. Acceptance: a reproducible red test (per-exit-path leftovers survive today), the record-and-reap implementation in both hosts, three idempotent start-quit cycles with the leftover count at zero and foreign applications' WebKit untouched, and the V5-109 record corrected. Done on 2026-09-30: both hosts record the pids of the WebKit XPC they create into `webkit-children.json` in their configuration directory (Chromium SingletonLock precedent — own territory, own record) and re-appraise the record on every page load, so WebKit's replacement of a killed child is followed. At startup, before creating any WebKit, a host kills only a recorded child that is alive, still names a WebKit process (recycling guard), and whose start time matches the record, while a live sibling instance (`host_pid` alive and soksak) suspends reaping entirely; the pure decision is a paired contract test in both hosts (`webkit-children.reap.requires-alive-webkit-same-start`). Red: the case matrix (`e2e/webkit-reaping.mjs`, both applications) failed on every assertion — no record existed. Green: all ten assertions pass per application, three idempotent start-quit cycles of the release build hold the count flat, and the unrecorded decoy (a foreign-store WebKit lookalike) survives every path. The matrix covers partial-kill states beyond on/off cycles: an external kill of one child while the host lives (the record must follow the replacement), a crash with one recorded child already dead (the mixed state), and a recorded lookalike victim proving the kill path deterministically without waiting for the rare spawn race. Gates: `pnpm test`, `make docs-check`, `make host-parity-check`, `make native-test`, `make host-contract-check` (229/229) all pass; the V5-109 record is superseded by this entry.

A press inside another image region is now a region-to-region transition — the previously focused region reports its focus loss and hands the first responder to the pressed region in the same event pass, so the page webview never holds the keyboard and the address field's stale active element is never refocused. Red: the native activation test pressed region B while region A held the responder and the responder ended on the page webview (B never reported its gain); the synthetic-pointer e2e path cannot reproduce this — the responder churn is AppKit real-event routing, and the probe built on `input.pointer` was measuring nothing (kept as an end-state regression check with its claim corrected). Both hosts call the same `activateWindow` in `native/darwin/src/input_inject.m`, which uses `activateIgnoringOtherApps:`. Measurement on three fresh launches: the host's own request (`activateIgnoringOtherApps:`) was refused 3/3 while another application stayed frontmost, and `NSRunningApplication activateWithOptions:` from the check process activated the same host 3/3. Cause: macOS cooperative activation refuses the self-activation of an application that the user has not activated since its background launch. Correction: `Session.pointer` with `activate` first activates the host through `activateApp` (`NSRunningApplication`) from the check process, as a person switching to it does, and the host request then completes the key window and webview steps; docs/spec/exposure.md states the rule. Make the test environment able to mount a native surface (the `native` flag is fixed at import), establish owning Red, then reject the composition wait with the mount error. Green: the test passes and workbench passes 204/204. Disposing that failed surface rethrows the mount error and leaves the surface (V5-117-1-3-4-7-1-7-3) (macOS 26.6.2 arm64).

Establish owning Red, then let disposal wait for the mount to settle and finish its cleanup, keeping the mount error reported where the mount failed. Red: the new `packages/workbench/test/surface-dispose-failed.test.mjs` mounts a native hybrid surface whose module throws and disposes it; on the unchanged module `disposeSurface` rejects with `fixture mount failed`. Correction: disposal of an authorized surface without a module waits for the mount to settle with `Promise.allSettled` and then removes the exposure, the host element, the authorization and the `mounted` entry; the mount error stays reported by the surface status and the caller of `mountSurface`. ## Tauri/Wails parity audit (2026-09-21)

The mechanical host check reports `apps/tauriv2/test/runtime.test.mjs: no counterpart in apps/wailsv3`. This remains a file-structure mismatch. Wails tests `waitPresented` dispatch in `runtime-contract.test.mjs`, and G2.5 now asserts the returned `{ displayed: 42 }` value through both adapters; the missing filename alone does not establish missing behavior coverage.

The bounded diagnostic capture contract is now symmetric for the current macOS hosts. Both `diagnostics.capture.stop` implementations return `frames`, `count`, `limited`, and `longestGap`; the Wails platform adapter reads the shared macOS cap state, and its payload tests cover capped and uncapped results. The shared macOS capture implementation and the recording state tests remain separate from gesture-completeness measurement: `limited: true` is normal, while a gesture whose end was not recorded fails measurement.

At the 2026-09-21 audit snapshot, the modal implementation had a larger confirmed gap. Tauri's `modals::show` created a child native WebView, loaded `/overlay.html`, kept it hidden until `ready`, then applied the mode-specific background, raised it, and focused it. At that snapshot Wails `OverlayShow` only stored modal state and emitted `modal-content`; it did not create or load a modal WebView, and Wails' `ConfigureModal` and `FocusModal` methods had no call site. That Red established an implementation gap, not an appearance-only test failure. The later F10.2 correction creates the Wails child-WebView contract; its current rebuilt-host evidence is recorded in F10.2 and remains subject to the wider F10 gate.

The host test file sets otherwise have matching names, including `recording_test`. The structure checker accumulates differences; it does not stop at that runtime file. Matching names do not establish matching behavior. The previous 27-track source-glob audit omits native bridge languages outside its fixed roots and does not execute behavior checks; its pass is not feature-parity evidence.

The real-session PTY close test failed with `No such process` when closing an already-exited child. After checking and reaping that child explicitly, the same two-session test passes without skipping. Full service reconnect, descendant cleanup, and repeated-close resource measurements remain pending.

## Earlier validation

Terminal keyboard forwarding is corrected on macOS (2026-09-20). Tauri's empty image-event callback discarded native input; the terminal plugin also discarded the character of modified keys in both hosts. Before correction, the three-terminal native-input test failed ordinary typing in Tauri and Ctrl+U in Wails. After correction, both rebuilt hosts passed all eight test cases (two parent cases and six terminal cases), with no failures or skips: native click, character input, Backspace, Ctrl+U, Enter, exactly-once command output, and isolation from the other terminals. `terminal.screen` publishes sidecar screen notifications; checks no longer repeatedly request screen content. Native tests, package tests, both builds, and structural checks passed. These results validate keyboard input, not the remaining composition failures. The originally reported window was preserved.

Current composition verification (2026-09-21, macOS 26.6.2) is green for the rebuilt-host scope recorded here. The baseline Wails build reproduced shell white pixels and terminal boundary intrusion. The cause of the Wails empty-terminal failure was a missing `compositionDeclare` registration and immutable declaration path; the host now rejects undeclared placement and records the declaration before placement. Rebuilt Tauri and Wails runs each passed the three-terminal project-return test and the fixed-cell rapid-divider test. The tests require actual movement, six round trips, three terminal regions in every capture, no white pixels or border intrusion, stable glyph metrics, and restored terminal/session identity. `make -C native/darwin test`, `make docs-check`, and `git diff --check` pass. This does not establish the remaining process-lifecycle, cursor, OSC, IME, or loading requirements.

Current-HEAD confirmation (2026-09-21, macOS 26.6.2): binaries built from `660d176` passed the same three-terminal rapid-divider and project-return test independently in Tauri (1/1, 6.14s) and Wails (1/1, 5.42s). The Wails process log reported `vcs.revision=660d176`. These results establish the two-host composition behavior for that built revision only; they do not close the remaining runtime, cursor, protocol, IME, or restoration requirements.

Contracts: [projects and settings](spec/projects.md), [layout](../packages/soksak/docs/layout.md), [surface placement](spec/native-surfaces.md), [native modals](spec/native-modals.md). Procedures: [build and verify](operations/examples.md).

Library simplification verification on 2026-09-08 rebuilt and restarted both macOS hosts. The full example run passed 37 checks, failed 2 recording checks for insufficient frame counts (Wails 56, Tauri 55; more than 60 required), and skipped 2 display-transition checks because only one 2× display was connected. The two failed checks passed when rerun with the same code and criteria. Frame-count reliability remains intermittent; this change does not correct it. Go 3/3 and Rust 3/3 storage tests and `make docs-check` passed. Windows/Linux native execution is unverified. The unchanged layout library retains its `1a921b4` validation: 310 tests passed and all 142 mutations detected.

Recording completeness (2026-09-17): the capture writes frames on a separate queue and `diagnostics.capture.stop` reports the longest display gap; drag recordings fail above 100ms. Before this, disk writes of up to 480ms at 2× dropped frames and caused the intermittent frame-count failures noted above. Window resize and maximize are measured by `resize.test.mjs`; the layout follows the window frame 250–400ms late during the AppKit or Wails animation (WebKit/WebKit#72971, tauri-apps/tao#1207), and the settled frame matches the window size.
